Wider Sports News.summary: Owner of WSL club says contract value exceeds Atlanta NWSL team’s US$4m-a-year Aflac deal. The post Michele Kang: London City’s Nike shirt deal ‘worth more’ than some in Premier League appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Women’s Super League (WSL) club London City Lionesses have signed a front-of-shirt sponsorship deal with Nike which the club’s owner Michele Kang has hailed as the biggest in women’s soccer.

Terms of the multi-year deal were not disclosed but Kang told BBC Sport that the contract is worth more than some shirt deals in the men’s Premier League. Previous reports have suggested that the most valuable shirt deal in the women’s game belongs to the new National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) franchise in Atlanta, who have partnered with insurance company Aflac ahead of their debut season in 2028.

Wider Sports News.title: ”Invest in Ukraine”: Rinat Akhmetov’s SCM issues a global call to international community for UEFA Champions League season
Wider Sports News.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk is turning its Champions League presence into a platform for economic diplomacy, using football’s global reach to encourage international investment in Ukraine and reinforce the case for rebuilding while the war continues. The post ”Invest in Ukraine”: Rinat Akhmetov’s SCM issues a global call to international community for UEFA Champions League season appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Kyiv, August 31, 2026 – Ukraine’s largest private investor — Rinat Akhmetov’s System Capital Management (SCM) companies — is launching a global communications initiative calling on international business to invest in Ukraine. As part of the initiative, Shakhtar Donetsk Football Club will play the league phase of the 2026/2027 UEFA Champions League in shirts carrying the call to “Invest in Ukraine.”

The league phase of the UEFA Champions League is one of the world’s most prominent sporting platforms, attracting one of the largest audiences. The club will play at least eight matches against leading European clubs, while the Ukrainian champions will host their home matches in London — one of the world’s financial capitals.

Wider Sports News.summary: As betting operators adapt to shifting regulatory environments, data from the TSC SPIN 100 shows how investors are responding differently to companies attempting to navigate the change. The post Betting beyond front-of-shirt: Why investors are split on the gambling industry’s next move appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The 2026/27 Premier League season began on 21st August with one obvious commercial change. No betting company appeared on the front of a club’s matchday shirt as part of the new voluntary league-wide ban.

The decision was made in 2023, when Premier League clubs collectively agreed to remove gambling sponsors from the front of their kits. Operators and clubs have therefore had three years to prepare.

Wider Sports News.title: Unrivaled: What does startup league’s US$650m valuation say about the future of women’s basketball?
Wider Sports News.summary: After only its second season, three-on-three women’s basketball league Unrivaled has landed US$100 million in additional funding. The post Unrivaled: What does startup league’s US$650m valuation say about the future of women’s basketball? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
American women’s basketball is having a moment. Audiences and attendances are up league-wide in the Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA), with a record All-Star Game crowd in Chicago exceeding that of its NBA equivalent this year.

Then late in August Unrivaled, the three-on-three startup league co-founded by WNBA stars Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart in 2023, secured US$100 million of Series C funding to take its estimated valuation to US$650 million. Stacked with high-profile and celebrity investors, its latest oversubscribed capital raise came less than a year after a Series B round that pegged its worth at US$340 million.

This year’s event will feature an expanded programme of sport, live music, entertainment, family activities and hospitality experiences. The three-day event brought together attendees from across the UAE and around the world in Dubai.

Rugby.title: Fissler Confidential: Jacques Nienaber's Leinster plot twist?
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter says that the chances of Wallaby superstar Len Ikitau returning to Sandy Park after the 2027 World Cup in Australia are hanging in the balance.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter says that the chances of Wallaby superstar Len Ikitau returning to Sandy Park after the 2027 World Cup in Australia are hanging in the balance. Outside centre Ikitau spent last season in Devon, making 13 appearances and scoring four tries, but Baxter brought in Will Butt from Bath, while Dallas McLeod will arrive at the club following the NPC.

“We had some very early discussions, but it’s probably too early to say any more than that. We brought in Dallas, and we’ll see how our young players go, because that may have sealed off the squad for Len,” he said.

Rugby.title: The former England U18 star thriving after taking a chance in New Zealand
Rugby.summary: Worboys scored 23 points, kicking nine goals from nine attempts: five penalties and four conversions, as Manawatu snapped North Harbour’s three-game winning streak.
Rugby.body:
George Worboys has found an unlikely rugby home in Palmerston North. The former England Under-18 first five, who passed through the prestigious Bath Rugby Academy and played in the senior team with the British and Irish Lions ten Finn Russell, is thriving for Manawatu in the NPC.

After making a big impact from the bench in Manawatu’s improbable 36-35 comeback win against Southland on August 8, he started the next three games. On Saturday, Worboys scored 23 points, kicking nine goals from nine attempts: five penalties and four conversions, as Manawatu snapped North Harbour’s three-game winning streak 43-40.

Rugby.summary: The injury rumours that circulated in the media earlier in the week about Carter Gordon have proven to be incorrect.
Rugby.body:
The injury rumours that circulated in the media earlier in the week about Carter Gordon have proven to be incorrect, but that doesn’t erase the discourse that followed the reporting.

Gordon has had an injury-riddled return to rugby since his stint in the NRL, and it has put a strain on the Wallaby playmaking stocks. It’s clear that there is no preferred or trusted back-up to Gordon currently in the Wallabies squad, and coach Les Kiss cannot afford to be sentimental; he must deal with the issue at hand.

Rugby.title: How Ultimate Sevens aims to supercharge the profile of rugby stars
Rugby.summary: When it comes to global sports, few things get bums on seats more than a celebrity star player signing.
Rugby.body:
When it comes to global sports, few things get bums on seats more than a celebrity star player signing. While in the past, rugby has been slower to the table compared to the likes of football when it comes to leaning to that star power, the last few years has seen that change, the likes of France’s Antoine Dupont and the USA’s Ilona Maher commanding significant profiles.

Showing athletes not just for their skill on the field, but their personality off it has become a primary goal for the inaugural season of the Ultimate Sevens, the competition sparing no expense in getting some of the biggest names in the short format of the game.

Rugby.title: Kolisi urges Boks to channel spirit of Soweto to beat All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Captain Siya Kolisi calls on the Springboks to summon inspiration from Soweto's pivotal part in South Africa's history as they host New Zealand on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Captain Siya Kolisi has called on the Springboks to summon inspiration from Soweto's pivotal part in South Africa's history as they take on New Zealand on the edge of the Johannesburg township on Saturday.

The 94,736-capacity FNB Stadium staged the opening match of football's World Cup, the first and only time the tournament has been staged in Africa. However, Kolisi, South Africa's first black captain, also referenced 1976's Soweto Uprising - the student protests that were a turning point in the fight against apartheid, the state-backed racial segregation of South African society.

Rugby.title: The auditions start now: One year to go until the first British & Irish Lions Women tour
Rugby.summary: There is exactly one year to go until the British & Irish Lions Women play their first tour match in New Zealand.
Rugby.body:
There is exactly one year to go until the British & Irish Lions Women play their first tour match in New Zealand. By then the British & Irish Lions Women will have been a project more than six years in the making. Now it is 12 months away from becoming a reality.

It is a team that was launched after a feasibility study that took just shy of three years before it was announced a team would come into existence, and give the top players from England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales the opportunity to compete together under one banner for the very first time. A game changer for women’s rugby.

Rugby.summary: 2026 FISU World University Championship Rugby Sevens BC Rugby News
Rugby.body:
Canada are undefeated after wins over Botswana 70-0 and Ireland 35-7, they’ll face Australia to complete pool play on Day 2. Australia were upset by Ireland 22-19 on Day 1 leaving Canada as the only 2-0 team in Pool B. France and Japan are undefeated in Pool A. The quarter-finals take place on Day 2 following the last pool match.

Two Canadian players were named in the Players to Watch on the official FISU website. Canada’s Ava Ference has been central to her side’s unbeaten start, accumulating 22 points through 11 successful conversions. Her accuracy from the tee has complemented Canada’s attacking strength and helped the Canadians establish themselves as early favourites in the women’s competition.

Rugby.title: 'I’m not one to keep secrets': Swys de Bruin lifts the lid on his abrupt Springbok Women exit
Rugby.summary: Swys de Bruin has opened up about his abrupt departure as head coach of the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Swys de Bruin has opened up about his shock exit as head coach of the Springbok Women. This week, ahead of the team’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry clash with the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium, rumours emerged that De Bruin had resigned.

Later, when the Boks announced their match day 23 for the Soweto fixture, SA Rugby confirmed that the 66-year-old had left his post. During his two years in charge – which De Bruin described as “wonderful” – the former Lions and Springbok Men attack coach led his team to the knockout stages of a Women’s Rugby World Cup for the first time ever.

Rugby.title: The emergence of softly-spoken Peter Lakai within the All Blacks environment
Rugby.summary: Quiet characters are easy to find in the All Blacks environment, far more so than outspoken ones. But even by New Zealand's standards, Peter Lakai stands out as especially laid-back and undisturbed.
Rugby.body:
Quiet characters are easy to find in the All Blacks environment, far more so than outspoken ones. But even by New Zealand standards, Peter Lakai stands out as especially laid-back and undisturbed.

The 23-year-old is in his third season with the national team, having generated All Blacks buzz with his New Zealand Age Grade Player of the Year Award in 2022 after debuting and starring for the Wellington Lions as a teenager. Lakai has since established himself as a non-negotiable selection in the All Blacks’ matchday 23, thanks in large part to his remarkable consistency for such a young athlete.

Rugby.title: New family dynasty set for special piece of Test history in Soweto
Rugby.summary: The Sititi family will take centre stage at FNB Stadium on Saturday, with 19-year-old sensation Amarante named for the Black Ferns and 23-year-old brother Wallace named for the All Blacks in the Greatest Rivalry double-header.
Rugby.body:
The Sititi family will take centre stage at FNB Stadium on Saturday, with 19-year-old sensation Amarante named for the Black Ferns and 23-year-old brother Wallace named for the All Blacks in the Greatest Rivalry double-header.

It’s just the second time siblings have represented New Zealand on the same day, following Annaleah and Xavier Rush in 1998. Both siblings have been named in the No.20 jerseys for their respective teams, with Amarante set to make just her second Test appearance for the Black Ferns and Wallace in line to make his 22nd Test appearance for the All Blacks.

Rugby.body:
Springboks captain Siya Kolisi has urged supporters to flock to FNB Stadium for the Springbok Women’s match with the Black Ferns. This weekend, South Africa’s biggest stadium will see the Springbok Women and the six-time world champion Black Ferns go toe-to-toe for just the third time. Ever. The fixture will also be the curtain-raiser to the third Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

To date, the Springbok Women and Black Ferns have played each other just twice. The last of those encounters came just shy of a year ago in a Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final in Exeter.

Rugby.title: Singleton hopes for rugby union return after heart attack
Rugby.summary: Jack Singleton hopes to return to rugby union and is looking for a new club, a year after suffering a heart attack.
Rugby.body:
A year after suffering a heart attack, hooker Jack Singleton is hoping to return to full training next month to get his rugby union career back on track. Singleton had played one Prem Cup game for Gloucester in September 2025, as the 2025-26 campaign was getting under way, when he had the heart attack aged 29 while training at the club.

"We're not really sure when it started but it wasn't like a scary moment for me, it was just a lot of symptoms or dizziness [and an] aching arm," he told BBC Radio Gloucestershire.

Rugby.title: Club legend emerges as favourite to replace Leo Cullen at Leinster
Rugby.summary: Cullen has been in charge of Leinster since 2015.
Rugby.body:
Felipe Contepomi has emerged as the favourite to make a romantic return to Leinster to replace Leo Cullen when he stands down at the end of the season. Argentina’s all-time leading points scorer, Contepomi, 49, is regarded as one of Leinster’s club legends after spending six years at the RDS as a player and a further four on the coaching staff before leaving in 2023 to return to Argentina.

He first served as an assistant to Michael Cheika at the 2023 World Cup, then took over the top job, and now Leinster, who have drawn up a shortlist he heads, will have to try to tempt him away.

Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women could leap three places up the World Rugby rankings with a shock win against the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium. On Saturday, the Springbok Women and Black Ferns will play one another as part of a doubleheader in Soweto. The fixture acts as a curtain-raiser to the Springboks and All Blacks‘ third Test in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

Any victory for the Springbok Women will see them move three places up the World Rugby rankings from 10th to seventh. An additional place is up for grabs if South Africa win by 15 points or more.

Rugby.title: 'They don't play hide and seek': Springboks react to All Blacks' selection tweaks
Rugby.summary: The Springboks say the All Blacks have sent a message with their selections for the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series, and that message has been received loud and clear.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks say the All Blacks have sent a message with their selections for the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series, and that message has been received loud and clear.

New Zealand selectors have turned to some fresh bodies for the must-win Soweto Test, knowing a loss this week would eliminate their chances of a series win. The tweaks have all come in the forward pack, where Asafo Aumua, Sam Darry and Peter Lakai have been injected into the starting lineup at the expense of Codie Taylor, Simon Parker and Fabian Holland, although the latter has remained in the matchday 23.

Rugby.title: What Rob Baxter wants to see from Tommy Wyatt's long-awaited comeback
Rugby.summary: Wyatt, 26, who can play in any of the back-five positions, last played for the Chiefs in a home defeat to Sale Sharks in May 2025.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter wants to see full-back Tommy Wyatt play with a smile on his face when he makes his long-awaited comeback on Saturday. Wyatt is set to end his two-year injury hell after being named on the bench for the friendly at Sandy Park.

The 26-year-old, who can play in any of the back-five positions, last played for the Chiefs in a home defeat to Sale Sharks in May 2025. He damaged ligaments to his right knee early in 2024 in a game against Glasgow and then suffered the same fate to his left knee in the final game of the 2024/25 season, which led to him missing the whole of last year’s campaign.

Rugby.summary: The Oranje Dames XV have named the squad that will compete in the WXV Global Series Challenger this month.
Rugby.body:
The Oranje Dames XV have named the squad that will compete in the WXV Global Series Challenger this month. The Netherlands prepared for their trip to Hong Kong China with a 33-0 win over a Scotland A team coached by Claire Cruikshank.

Linde van der Velden scored a brace in Amsterdam, while Mariet Luijken and Esmee Ligtvoet were also try scorers last Saturday. It was the final home fixture for the team’s head coach, Gareth Gilbert, who will return to his native South Africa after the WXV Global Series Challenger.

Rugby.summary: With no annoying league table to offer a crushing reality check, a swirling world of possibilities await every club for the campaign ahead.
Rugby.body:
The start of the English rugby season may have been put back by a fortnight for the rank and file because of the summer heatwave and its effect on the playing surfaces up and down the country, but the top end will get under way this weekend with the Prem Cup.

To be honest the Prem Cup is more of a tip-toe than a leap into the new season even if Bristol v Gloucester on Saturday will be televised on TNT Sports. The competition is a pale imitation of the domestic cup whose final used to fill Twickenham in its glory days.

Rugby.summary: As Yaras head coach Guilherme Coghetto has confirmed his squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for the WXV Global Series Challenger.
Rugby.body:
As Yaras head coach Guilherme Coghetto has confirmed his squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for the WXV Global Series Challenger. The former assistant coach has included 11 players with Olympic Games experience, as well as 16 players who represented Brazil at last year’s Women’s Rugby World Cup in England.

Across three weeks, Brazil will play fixtures against Hong Kong China, the Netherlands and Spain. It will be the first time ever that As Yaras have played Hong Kong China, while they have taken on the Netherlands five times previously and Las Leonas once.

Rugby.summary: Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl says Taulupe Faletau has returned to non-contact training and thinks he will still want to play for Wales.
Rugby.body:
Cardiff are hopeful that Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau will be fit for the start of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC). The 35-year-old suffered a season-ending shoulder injury at Sharks in March, and was limited to just seven appearances in the past campaign after knee and calf issues earlier in the campaign.

Faletau has featured in pre-season training and will soon step up his comeback in the build-up to the URC opener against Scarlets on Saturday, 26 September (19:45 BST). Head coach Corniel van Zyl said: "Even though he can't do contact, he can still run so fitness-wise he's in a good space.

Rugby.summary: Scarlets suffer blow before new United Rugby Championship season with the loss of summer signing Chris Apoua to an Achilles injury.
Rugby.body:
Scarlets have released summer signing Chris Apoua after the forward ruptured an Achilles in training. The 34-year-old tight-head prop signed for the Llanelli-based club in August from Super Rugby side Moana Pasifika.

But the veteran, who has played provincial rugby in New Zealand with Northland and Southland, suffered a serious injury soon after linking up with Nigel Davies' squad and will miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Rugby.title: All Blacks prop George Bower has message for the Bok scrum
Rugby.summary: All Blacks loosehead George Bower has made it clear he does not fear packing down against the Springboks in the third Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry test in Soweto...
Rugby.body:
All Blacks loosehead George Bower has made it clear he does not fear packing down against the Springboks in the third Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry test in Soweto and is relishing another head-to-head that could have a major bearing on the result.

With the series tied 1-1 after the Springboks won the second test after losing the opener, the scrum has become the focal point for both coaches after All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie accused the Boks of walking around the scrum. Opposite number Rassie Erasmus responded strongly in defence of his players and all week the home side has dismissed the All Blacks attacks.

Rugby.summary: Japan head coach Eddie Jones has made five changes to the starting XV that crashed to a 56-17 defeat to Australia three weeks ago for Saturday's Centenary Test against Canada in Niigata City.
Rugby.body:
Japan head coach Eddie Jones has made five changes to the starting XV that crashed to a 56-17 defeat to Australia three weeks ago for Saturday’s Centenary Test against Canada in Niigata City.

Notably, captain and lock Warner Dearns is out as one of three changes to the pack, with Jack Cornelsen named as Harry Hockings’ partner in the second row. Scrum-half Naoto Saito takes on the armband in the absence of Dearns. Saito has captained the Brave Blossoms twice before, against Uruguay and England in 2024.

Rugby.title: Danelle Lochner: 'We’re a much better team than the one that lost last year'
Rugby.summary: For 15 minutes between the two halves of their Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final against New Zealand, South Africa were in dreamland.
Rugby.body:
For 15 minutes between the two halves of their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final against New Zealand, South Africa were in dreamland. A side that had never been in the knockouts of the game’s premier competition were all square at 10-10 with the team who had lifted the trophy more than any other. But South Africa weren’t hanging on.

They had dominated the opening 40 minutes against the Black Ferns, scoring two tries through rumbling forward play and dynamic running off the shoulder and around the corner. The maul was thrumming. The breakdown was immense. If anything, they deserved a lead.

Rugby.body:
Ben Carter and Angus O’Brien have been named Dragons RFC co-captains for the 2026/27 season – the Newport-Gwent-based URC outfit has confirmed. The pair will share the role for a third consecutive campaign, having led the Welsh region in the United Rugby Championship and EPCR Challenge Cup over the past two seasons.

They will be supported by Harrison Keddie, Aneurin Owen, Matthew Screech and Thomas Young, who form part of the club’s senior leadership group. Head Coach Filo Tiatia said: “I’m delighted to confirm Ben and Angus will continue to lead us into the new season.

Rugby.title: Why Caluori played on with detached wrist ligament
Rugby.summary: Wing sensation Noah Caluori says he played through the pain of a torn wrist ligament during his break-out season for Saracens and England
Rugby.body:
Teenage wing sensation Noah Caluori has revealed that he spent the majority of his breakthrough season - featuring 18 tries in 13 Prem games and an England debut - playing with a detached ligament in his wrist.

The 19-year-old sustained the injury when he came down heavily on his arm while competing for a high ball in Saracens' defeat by Exeter in December. After consulting both club and national team coaches, Caluori opted to play through his pain and wait until the summer for an operation to reconnect the ligament.

Rugby.summary: USA U20s captain Spencer Huntley is no stranger to being the youngest rugby prospect in the room.
Rugby.body:
USA U20s captain Spencer Huntley is no stranger to being the youngest rugby prospect in the room. It’s a challenge the scrum-half became quite accustomed to throughout the age-grade ranks, before being named in an Eagles-heavy USA XV squad last month.

Huntley first got the chance to play for the USA U20s as a 17-year-old, before suiting up for the U23s at just 18. These weren’t opportunities Huntley was daunted by, with the teenager working hard to show “there’s a reason why I’m here.”

Rugby.summary: Beno Obano will become the latest England player to put his Test career on ice after agreeing to join French side Pau at the end of the forthcoming season.
Rugby.body:
Beno Obano will become the latest England player to put his Test career on ice with a move to France, after agreeing to join Top 14 side Pau from Bath at the end of the forthcoming season.

The 31-year-old loose-head prop won his fifth cap in the defeat by South Africa in July, backing up first-choice Ellis Genge off the bench. Rugby.title: Jake White: What people are reliably getting wrong about the scrum
Rugby.summary: Scrum debate: I’ll tell you a story. One that may give you context to the events of the past few days.
Rugby.body:
I’ll tell you a story. One that may give you context to the events of the past few days. In the famous 1949 New Zealand tour of South Africa – the one in which the Springboks whitewashed the All Blacks 4-0 – Danie ‘Doc’ Craven was the South Africa coach.

Back then, it took the tourists 26-days to travel by boat to South Africa, and even then, more boat travel was required to move from Test to Test. Legend has it that on one voyage, ‘Doc’ Craven, boarded the ship and assisted the travelling opponents in the art of scrummaging. Whether it was true or not is open to conjecture, but the story has grown legs over the last 77 years and is a parable about the foundations of the The Greatest Rivalry. Either way, what cannot be disputed is Doc’s authority as a visionary coach and man of outstanding virtue. Indeed, he played and captained the Springboks pre-war. He coached Stellenbosch and the Springboks for seven years and as an administrator was SARU President and IRB (World Rugby) Chairman, all while being a noted author on rugby strategy and tactics. He did it all.

Rugby.title: Statement: SA Rugby confirm the future of Springbok Women boss Swys de Bruin
Rugby.summary: SA Rugby have confirmed that Swys de Bruin has stepped away as head coach of the Springbok Women two days before their Rugby's Greatest Rivalry match with the Black Ferns.
Rugby.body:
SA Rugby have confirmed that Swys de Bruin has stepped away as head coach of the Springbok Women two days before their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry match with the Black Ferns. In the interim, assistant coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September have been announced as co-head coaches. The pair have led South Africa to title success at this year’s Rugby Africa Women’s Cup in Kenya, and in their tour whitewash of the Fijiana XV.

SA Rugby, in their squad announcement, said: “Media are advised that Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September, who led the team to success in Kenya and Fiji earlier this year, will continue to act as co-head coaches of the Springbok Women’s team following the decision by Swys de Bruin to step down from the role. No further comment will be made in the short-term to allow the team to focus on their match with New Zealand’s Black Ferns.”

Rugby.title: Why the smart money should be on rugby sevens
Rugby.summary: Why the smart money should be on rugby sevens City AM
Rugby.body:
Why should we be taking more notice of rugby sevens at the moment, asks former player Jim Hamilton. There are different versions of rugby, and while the 15-a-side game will always be my Everest, sevens offers something completely different. The sport is simple to follow, fast and incredibly athletic, and it allows individual personalities and athletes to shine in a way that can be harder in 15s. But the opportunity of rugby sevens goes well beyond what happens on the pitch.

Sevens has always had the travel, entertainment and experience built into it from the start – Hong Kong and Cape Town come to mind as great destinations. Anyone who has been to either of those tournaments understands that you are not simply getting a ticket to watch rugby but buying into a weekend and a host city.

Rugby.summary: Former Wallabies backrower Isi Naisarani has secured a Super Rugby Pacific homecoming after inking a deal with the Fijian Drua.
Rugby.body:
Former Wallabies backrower Isi Naisarani has secured a Super Rugby Pacific homecoming after inking a deal with the Fijian Drua for the 2027 season. Fiji-born Naisarani previously played for three Australian Super Rugby clubs before heading overseas to Japan.

Naisarani started out at Super Rugby level almost 10 years ago with the Western Force, becoming the first player to win the coveted Nathan Sharpe Medal (Force Player of the Year) as a rookie, having featured in 15 matches that season.

Rugby.title: Triston Reilly to captain First Nations & Pasifika XV in historic match
Rugby.summary: ACT Brumbies recruit Triston Reilly will captain the First Nations & Pasifika XV in a historic clash with a Tonga President’s XV.
Rugby.body:
ACT Brumbies recruit Triston Reilly will captain the First Nations & Pasifika XV in a historic clash with a Tonga President’s XV at Teufaiva Stadium, which will be the inaugural contest for the Kaume’a Ofi Trophy (meaning ‘Close friends’ in Tongan).

Reilly scored a try for the FNP side against the British & Irish Lions 14 months ago, falling short of a win in a hard-fought match at Melbourne’s Marvel Stadium. The FNP concept returned earlier this year, when a side was named to compete at the Hong Kong 10s in April.

Rugby.summary: Record-breaking front-rower James Slipper is returning for another season with the ACT Brumbies.
Rugby.body:
Record-breaking front-rower James Slipper is returning for another season with the ACT Brumbies, with the all-time Wallabies and Super Rugby appearance leader signing on for the 2027 campaign.

Slipper is the most-capped player in Super Rugby history, going clear of the long-held tally held by former Crusaders prop Wyatt Crockett. ‘Slips’ also stands alone as the all-time appearance leader for the Wallabies, having played 154 Tests in gold.

Rugby.summary: Northampton boss Phil Dowson says he is optimistic about extending Henry Pollock's contract despite agent demands for seven-figure annual wages.
Rugby.body:
Northampton boss Phil Dowson says he is relaxed about boxing supremo Eddie Hearn's ambition to secure Saints star Henry Pollock a contract extension worth a million pound a year.

Hearn, who signed a deal to secure commercial deals for Pollock in April, told the Daily Telegraph, external earlier this year that 21-year-old is "a seven-figure player" who "cannot stay at this club on the money he's on".

Rugby.title: Exeter make cross-code swoop for Sydney-based RL winger
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs have signed winger/full-back Charlie Poynton from the South Sydney Rabbitohs for the 2026/27 season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs have signed winger/full-back Charlie Poynton from the South Sydney Rabbitohs for the 2026/27 season. The 19-year-old, who was born in New Zealand, will provide cover for the injured Paul Brown-Bampoe and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, who is on a break after international duty.

Poynton is no stranger to rugby union, having been part of the NSW Waratahs senior academy and played for their partner club, Manly Marlins. At international level, in July 2024 Poynton was selected in the Australia U18s development squad by coach Shannon Fraser.

Rugby.title: What happened the last time the Springbok Women played the Black Ferns?
Rugby.summary: When the Springbok Women and Black Ferns meet in Rugby's Greatest Rivalry this Saturday it will have been 357 days since their last meeting.
Rugby.body:
When the Springbok Women and Black Ferns meet in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry this Saturday it will have been 357 days since their last meeting. This weekend the teams will meet at FNB Stadium in Soweto. Their time shared on the field of South Africa’s largest stadium will be the warm-up act to the Springboks and All Blacks‘ third Test.

As things stand, the Test series between the two teams are finely poised. Last weekend, Rassie Erasmus’ side levelled things at one game apiece with a resurgent performance at DHL Stadium in Cape Town.

Rugby.title: Summer off England duty took me by surprise
Rugby.summary: England captain Maro Itoje says he was initially taken aback by the suggestion he step away from international action for the July Tests
Rugby.body:
England captain Maro Itoje says he was initially shocked when head coach Steve Borthwick raised the possibility of him taking the summer off. Itoje missed England's matches against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina in July, holidaying in Mauritius and Nigeria as he took a first proper summer break from professional rugby in more than a decade.

The 31-year-old, whose mother died in the weeks before he led England through a deflating Six Nations campaign that featured just one win, says he is now feeling the benefits of his time away.

Rugby.title: Maro Itoje admits to being taken aback by Steve Borthwick's novel idea
Rugby.summary: The England and Lions skipper says Borthwick first approached him after the Six Nations to discuss taking the summer off after exceeding the recommended 30-game-a-season limit in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns.
Rugby.body:
Maro Itoje admits he was taken aback when England boss Steve Borthwick suggested after the Six Nations that he miss the Nations Championship this summer. The England and Lions skipper says Borthwick first approached him after the Six Nations to discuss taking the summer off after exceeding the recommended 30-game-a-season limit in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns.

Itoje says that the more he thought about it, however, the more it made sense, and he is now firing on all cylinders once again ahead of the new season after completing his first full pre-season with Saracens in 12 years.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women and Catha Jacobs target another step forward against Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women utility forward Catha Jacobs believes time spent playing sevens has helped her in Test rugby.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women utility forward Catha Jacobs believes time spent playing sevens has helped her in Test rugby. In the wake of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 and her team’s quarter-final defeat to the Black Ferns, Jacobs was drafted into the Springbok Women’s Sevens squad for HSBC SVNS 2 and HSBC SVNS World Championship events.

Since those SVNS World Championship tournaments Jacobs has started in three of the Springbok Women’s last four Tests against the USA Women’s Eagles and Fiji. Ahead of this weekend’s one-off clash with New Zealand as part of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry – a fixture that acts as a warm-up to the third Test between the Springboks and All Blacks at FNB Stadium – Jacobs will get to display her refined skillset in front of home supporters in Soweto, against the second-ranked team win the world.

Rugby.summary: Sale Sharks director of rugby Alex Sanderson has backed Courtney Lawes to force his way back into the England squad this autumn after being hugely impressed by the veteran forward since his return to English rugby.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks director of rugby Alex Sanderson has backed Courtney Lawes to force his way back into the England squad this autumn after being hugely impressed by the veteran forward since his return to English rugby.

Lawes stepped away from the international game following the 2023 World Cup before joining Brive in 2024. But he is back in the Gallagher PREM now and has outlined his ambition to don the white jersey he has worn 105 times with the World Cup on the horizon, and Sanderson believes the 37-year-old remains capable of operating at Test level, insisting he “can’t see him not making the squad” if Steve Borthwick opens the door to a comeback.

Rugby.title: 'I think an Anglo-Welsh league would be brilliant': Rob Baxter
Rugby.summary: Ever since Cardiff and Swansea played rebel friendly fixtures against English sides in front of decent crowds in the late 90s, the idea of an Anglo-Welsh League has had plenty of support.
Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter has welcomed the idea of Welsh teams being included in an expanded Gallagher PREM, and his view is supported by other directors of rugby. Ever since Cardiff and Swansea played rebel friendly fixtures against English sides in front of decent crowds in the late 90s, the idea of an Anglo-Welsh League has had plenty of support.

And Baxter sees the mutual benefits of a cross-border competition, believing that it ‘ticks a lot of boxes’. “I think an Anglo-Welsh league would be brilliant, I’ve been a big advocate of it for years,” Baxter said at the launch of the new Gallagher PREM season at Alianz Stadium.

Rugby.summary: 2025 was the year that a new format was bestowed upon the world of HSBC SVNS.
Rugby.body:

Rugby.summary: After a frustrating Guinness Women’s Six Nations campaign you get the feeling that Scotland are determined to play some bold and exciting rugby during the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
After a frustrating Guinness Women’s Six Nations campaign you get the feeling that Scotland are determined to play some bold and exciting rugby during the WXV Global Series. And bold and exciting are two words that could be used to describe one of the squad’s up-and-coming talents in the shape of second row and back-row forward Holland Bogan.

She may just be 21, but the player who has come through the ranks at Cartha Queens Park, Stirling County and Glasgow Warriors is not shy in coming forward and has already become one of the real characters off the pitch within the international set-up in recent months.

Rugby.title: Seven potential debutants named as Italy look to ‘expand their player pool’ at WXV
Rugby.summary: New Italy head coach Plinio Sciamanna has named a 38-player Italy squad for the team's WXV Global Series campaign in September and October.
Rugby.body:
New Italy head coach Plinio Sciamanna has named a 38-player Italy squad for the team’s WXV Global Series campaign in September and October. The Azzurre will play home fixtures against Japan and South Africa, before a two-match tour of North America to take on the USA Women’s Eagles.

Sciamanna’s squad is comprised of 22 forwards and 16 backs. There are seven debutants included in the playing group. This includes Lyon lock Francesca Andreoli and her new club mate Mascia Jelic, Benetton hooker Silvia Fent, Milano prop Laura Moscato, Valsugana midfielder Natascia Aggio, Toulon back three Rubina Grassi and Valsugana fly-half Vittoria Zeni.

Rugby.title: Pauline Bourdon Sansus named France captain as key lock misses WXV Global Series
Rugby.summary: France head coach François Ratier has installed Pauline Bourdon Sansus as captain for the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:
France head coach François Ratier has installed Pauline Bourdon Sansus as captain for the WXV Global Series. The 30-year-old scrum-half takes the armband over from Manae Feleu, who misses the next two months of action to focus on her medicine studies.

Pauline Bourdon Sansus said: “A great sense of pride. Being captain of the French team is something exceptional, and it wasn’t necessarily something I was expecting. “But I’ve already held a leadership role in the team for a while, and Manae remains the captain; she’s the one who usually wears the armband. The two of us make a real team and complement each other well. It’s a bonus, but first and foremost I’m a rugby player, and my goal is to perform and help the team on the pitch.

Rugby.title: Childs play: Ex-South African schoolboy coach excited by new PREM challenge
Rugby.summary: From South African schoolboy rugby to the Stormers and now the PREM, Craig Childs is relishing his latest challenge.
Rugby.body:
Seven weeks in, Craig Childs is relishing his first senior defence coach job in professional rugby, having swapped University of Cape Town team Ikey Tigers for Leicester Tigers.

Childs’ work with Ikey Tigers in the Varsity Cup dovetailed with his role as pathways defence coach/assistant first team coach at the Stormers, which he held for three years working under Norman Laker, before accepting the opportunity to move overseas and become part of Geoff Parling’s coaching team.

Rugby.title: Johnnie Beattie: 'Royal Marines, sabotaged rowing machines and drinking from cement mixers' - a player's eye view of pre-season
Rugby.summary: From night watches on a Royal Air Force camp to scoffing oysters in the port of Montpellier, pre-season is a demanding, eventful and seminal period in the player's calendar.
Rugby.body:
The fear is palpable. Anxiety courses through the group, reducing some of the meanest, fittest and most muscular sportsmen on the planet to rubble. Questions bounce around your head like ricocheting bullets: what’s about to happen us? Will anything I do here impress the staff? Are my hamstrings going to survive? The sense of unknown and lack of control was too much for some boys to handle.

The first day of pre-season sends shivers down a rugby player’s spine like nothing else. It’s the most nervous and scared you will ever feel walking into a club. With the northern hemisphere pre-season in full swing, players across Europe and South Africa will have been wrestling with all the emotions and all the doubts I recall so vividly.

Rugby.title: Kiwi Christie chosen as Newcastle captain
Rugby.summary: New Zealand flanker Tom Christie is chosen as the new captain of Newcastle Red Bulls, replacing hooker George McGuigan.
Rugby.body:
Tom Christie has been named as Newcastle Red Bulls captain for the 2026-27 season. Kiwi flanker Christie, who joined the club last summer, captained Canterbury to success in New Zealand's National Provincial Championship in 2025, and was a three-time winner of Super Rugby with Crusaders before his move to the Prem.

The 28-year-old scored six tries in his 19 games for Red Bulls last season and replaces hooker George McGuigan as skipper. "Tom is an outstanding professional with natural leadership qualities," said, external Newcastle's new head coach Dan McFarland.

Rugby.title: Top 14 season 2026-27 preview: Which teams are tooled up to stop another Toulouse title?
Rugby.summary: The French top tier has flexed over the past two seasons, but Toulouse have been the one constant. Will the champions make history?
Rugby.body:
Fans of France’s Top 14 may notice a couple of crucial differences when the season kicks off on 5 September, as rule changes speed up penalties and conversions, and the flood of confusing second-half substitutions is cut to a relative trickle.

From the start of the new campaign, kickers will have 45 seconds to take penalties or convert tries, while an eight-year, 12 substitutions experiment has been ditched, as French professional club rugby comes back into line with the international eight-sub norm.

Rugby.title: Rugby Sevens comes to South Africa with excitement building for first-time hosts
Rugby.summary: Rugby Sevens comes to South Africa with excitement building for first-time hosts FISU
Rugby.body:

Hosted by University Sport South Africa and organised by Maties Sport at Stellenbosch University, the 2026 championship brings the competition to one of South Africa’s great university sporting environments. Rugby.summary: Nick Phipps has rated the Wallabies’ performance a seven to eight out of 10 after the 27-21 win over Los Pumas.
Rugby.body:
Nick Phipps has rated the Wallabies’ performance a seven to eight out of 10 after the 27-21 win over Los Pumas, but the 72-Test scrum-half believes the Argentinians will be back with a vengeance when the teams meet again.

It’s the fourth time the Aussies have taken out the first of two Tests away in Argentina, but the second match has historically gone the way of the home side. Los Pumas have been swept by the Wallabies in a multi-game series on home soil.

Rugby.title: All Blacks are primed to shock the world in Soweto
Rugby.summary: South Africa are potentially headed towards an ambush in Soweto. Erasmus' head is stuck in Cape Town, still going on about post-game comments on the Monday.
Rugby.body:
When Andre Esterhuizen snatched the ball for a clean steal to end the All Blacks chances of snatching a late draw in Cape Town, the relief became visible. After Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu booted the ball into the stands, nearly every Springbok player standing raised their arms triumphantly into the air. The contrast with the All Blacks in the first Test is clear.

Just one player was seen celebrating, Fabian Holland, while every other player was subdued and looked like they couldn’t care less on the surface. This visible release by the Boks looks like joy. It is, but also mixed with a healthy dose of relief. Facing extermination in the series the Cape Town Test presented an existential threat. Down 1-0, the Springboks simply had to win. They saved face. They could not face the prospect of being swept at home going into the third Test.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: The art of execution according to Quinn Tupaea
Rugby.summary: Of all the rugby clichés, one has been offered up to grieving All Blacks fans the most in the wake of recent losses.
Rugby.body:
Of all the rugby clichés, one has been offered up to grieving All Blacks fans the most in the wake of recent losses. Successive coaches have invoked the sentiment, unable to escape its relevance, and used it to cast the gap between success and failure as simple yet abstract.

“We created plenty of opportunities, we just couldn’t quite execute them.” As you read the words, you can no doubt picture a handful of people with a white fern on their chest speaking them. And while this new All Blacks group had managed to sing to a different tune thanks to eight straight wins to begin the 2026 season, the phrase inevitably reared its head in the wake of the weekend’s loss to the Springboks in Cape Town.

Rugby.title: 'How they have done it for years and years': Ex-All Black captain Read breaks down Springbok scrum
Rugby.summary: Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read has offered a detailed breakdown of the Springboks scrum which he claims has scrummed on an angle for "years and years".
Rugby.body:
Ex-All Black captain Kieran Read has offered a detailed breakdown of the Springboks scrum which he claims has scrummed on an angle for “years and years”. The former No.8 played South Africa 22 times over his international career, winning 16 times, with first hand knowledge of how the Springboks operate their scrum.

His last game against the Springboks was the 2019 Rugby World Cup pool game, won 23-13 by New Zealand, which featured a number of the current day forwards for South Africa. Read explained that the tendency of South Africa’s scrum has always been to scrum left and their tactic of isolating the tighthead for a “one-on-one” contest with the powerful Ox Nche.

Rugby.summary: Former England prop Shaunagh Brown is certain that the Red Roses are looking forward to a "proper challenge" in the WXV Global Series.
Rugby.body:

In September and October, England will play three Test matches against Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 runners-up Canada, as well as playing the Wallaroos, Black Ferns and USA Women’s Eagles once each.

In August, Red Roses head coach John Mitchell described the three fixtures against Canada as a “Test series” and that playing the same opposition three times “requires a little bit more unpredictability”.

Rugby.title: Beno Obano set to bring England career to a halt with Top 14 move
Rugby.summary: Bath have lost their battle to keep England loosehead Beno Obano at the Rec after he agreed a shock move to join Top 14 outfit Pau when his contract runs out next July.
Rugby.body:
Bath have lost their battle to keep England loosehead Beno Obano at the Rec after he agreed a shock move to join Top 14 outfit Pau when his contract runs out next July. It’s another blow for the former Gallagher PREM champions, who earlier lost their first-choice tighthead, Thomas Du Toit, who rejoined his former club, the Sharks, in Durban.

They also saw Alfie Barbeary move to Saracens, while François Van Wyk, who was Obano’s understudy, will be playing in the United Rugby Championship next season after moving to Connacht.

Rugby.title: ‘Not always easy to understand’: Bok scrum coach responds to accusations
Rugby.summary: South Africa scrum coach Daan Human has emphatically asserted that he has "never coached" his side to walk around in the scrum, adding that it is "not ideal for us".
Rugby.body:
South Africa scrum coach Daan Human has emphatically asserted that he has “never coached” his side to walk around in the scrum, adding that it is “not ideal for us”. Speaking to the media in the wake of the Springboks’ second Test victory over the All Blacks in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, Human defended his pack in light of accusations made by New Zealand boss Dave Rennie over alleged underhanded tactics in the scrum.

“The scrums were better tonight,” Rennie said after his side fell 33-26 in Cape Town to leave the four-match series level. “I think Angus was pretty strong around setting a mark and trying to keep the hookers in the same spacing.

Rugby.title: What is Australia’s first-choice team and how far does depth go, a year out from RWC27?
Rugby.summary: Les Kiss still has to settle on his optimum back-row combination, midfield pairing and back-up half-backs.
Rugby.body:
It was a really important win for Australia in Argentina, their fourth straight in 2026 and the first time they’ve enjoyed a streak this long since beating Portugal in their final match of RWC2023 – the end of the season to forget – and then winning their first three Tests under Joe Schmidt in 2024.

Schmidt’s Wallabies never won four in a row, but Les Kiss’s side can this Saturday in Mendoza. If they succeed, it would also see their overall streak – taking into account the win over Italy in Schmidt’s last Test – equal Dave Rennie’s run of five straight wins in 2021.

Rugby.summary: Two wins over South Africa 'A', 63 points scored and 31 conceded and a big momentum boost for the Yaras ahead of their first WXV Global Series Challenger participation.
Rugby.body:
Two wins over South Africa ‘A’, 63 points scored and 31 conceded and a big momentum boost for the Yaras ahead of their first WXV Global Series Challenger campaign. There’s no denying that Brazil has taken another step in their development since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, showcasing strong foundations in their game plan and a deeper squad better equipped to cope with the demands of any kind.

With the conclusion of the South Africa ‘A’ series, Brazil has recorded five wins – and just one defeat – since Guilherme Coghetto took charge of the women’s national team and programme. A more than promising sign ahead of their clashes against Hong Kong China, Netherlands and Spain.

Rugby.title: Spain boosted as award-winning scrum-half returns for WXV Global Series Challenger
Rugby.summary: Spain head coach Régis Sonnes has named the Las Leonas squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for WXV Global Series Challenger.
Rugby.body:
Spain head coach Régis Sonnes has named the Las Leonas squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for WXV Global Series Challenger. There is a Test rugby return for Anne Fernández de Corres on the cards. The scrum-half has not represented her country in 15-a-side rugby since Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, and represented the ACT Brumbies in Super Rugby Women’s earlier this year. During her time in Canberra she was named Helen Taylor Award for Women’s Player of the Year by the team.

Additionally, there are welcome returns to the squad for Alba Capell and Carmen Castellucci, who both missed the majority of the 2025/26 season with long-term injuries. Ahead of her time in Australia, the 28-year-old told RugbyPass: “By leaving my comfort zone, I have experienced some growth and self-development.

Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: 'They did not see the best of me': Vainah Ubisi vows to make her mark against Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: Vainah Ubisi has mixed memories of the Springboks' Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 campaign.
Rugby.body:
Vainah Ubisi has mixed memories of the Springboks‘ Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 campaign. On one hand, it was an historic occasion for South Africa as their women’s side reached the quarter-final stage of the tournament for the first time. On the other, she did not perform to the lofty standard she has set.

The 23-year-old lock, who has played in 26 Test matches already in her career, saw her preparation for last year’s Women’s Rugby World Cup curtailed by a knee injury. Instead of being utilised as a starter, Ubisi was used from the bench on three occasions. Including their quarter-final exit to the Black Ferns at Exeter’s Sandy Park.

Rugby.title: Gallagher PREM 2026/27 squads rated: Northampton Saints
Rugby.summary: George Furbank has been lost to Harlequins and James Ramm's versatility will be missed from the back three, but otherwise Saints have a largely settled and consistent group who know each other's game inside and out.
Rugby.body:

Rugby.summary: Some of the most moving social media content at Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 featured tearful Black Ferns bidding farewell to grief-stricken centre Amy du Plessis.
Rugby.body:
Some of the most moving social media content at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 featured tearful Black Ferns bidding farewell to grief-stricken centre Amy du Plessis. In the opening 54-8 win against Spain in York, she injured her shoulder after falling awkwardly in a tackle. She was due to return for the quarter-final agains South Africa, the country of her birth, but did not recover in time.

This weekend she has unfinished business in the historic first Test between the Black Ferns and Springbok Women at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg. “The game you love doesn’t always love you back,” Du Plessis told RugbyPass.

As one unrelenting hamster wheel of a season ends, another looms on the horizon. The United Rugby Championship begins on 25th September and already, new signings across rugby’s most geographically and tactically diverse league are bedding in.

At this point, that’s the most accurate we can be about Springboks team announcements. There are still more than 96 hours before kick-off in the third Test of the series against New Zealand and anything could change.

Rugby.title: Forget McZanno or McRizz; Tom Hooper has just blown that experiment out of the water
Rugby.summary: The debate about having McReight and Tizzano on the field together is moot, not to mention the conversation surrounding what the duo should be called.
Rugby.body:
There are a few key reasons why conventional No.7s are now an endangered species at Test level, and it is seeing selection pictures change course. The main reason for this move is that the breakdown turnover, also called the pilfer, or what is occasionally known as the jackal, is now a skill expected to be performed by several players, not just the player wearing the No.7 jersey.

Hookers with their athletic but stocky build traditionally have become a second pilfer option, but that mould never stopped All Blacks great Sam Whitelock from being a clutch jackaler.

Rugby.title: No one bought the Springboks' set piece charade
Rugby.summary: The mirage that was sold to the South African public was that this would be a one-sided series at scrum time. Those expectations were set on a false premise during those first 50 minutes.
Rugby.body:
The first Test in Johannesburg featured the most lopsided scrum in rugby history, with South Africa seemingly dominating the All Blacks on every feed. It looked like a masterclass in scrummaging and a demonstration of a weapon of mass destruction.

Once the reserve front rows came on, the scrum stabilised with no advantage to the Springboks for the final half hour. Then head coach Dave Rennie revealed that Ethan de Groot played through illness, coming down sick the night before.

Rugby.title: 'One-week wonders': Dave Rennie's All Blacks on World Rankings shortlist
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks' stay at the top of the World Rugby Men's Rankings only lasted one week after they fell to a 33-26 defeat to South Africa in the second Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series in Cape Town on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Only one week after climbing to No.1 in the World Rugby Men’s Rankings, the All Blacks were removed from their lofty perch by South Africa as a result of the Springboks’ 33-26 win in Cape Town in the second Test of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

In falling from grace so swiftly, they became only the fifth team in the 23-year history of the rankings to have the very briefest of stays as the world’s best team. Not that Dave Rennie cares a jot, he’s publicly said so.

Rugby.title: World Rugby statement: November's Nations Cup fixtures
Rugby.summary: World Rugby has confirmed the fixture schedule for the second phase of the inaugural Nations Cup, with 18 matches to be played across Europe and Hong Kong between November 6 and 21.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby has confirmed the fixture schedule for the second phase of the inaugural Nations Cup, with 18 matches to be played across Europe and Hong Kong between November 6 and 21.

Pool A consists of Canada, Chile, Samoa, Tonga, Uruguay and the USA. Pool B includes Georgia, Hong Kong China, Portugal, Romania, Spain and Zimbabwe. Teams play every nation from the opposite pool across the two international windows. At the conclusion of the six-round schedule, the team finishing top of each pool will be crowned inaugural Nations Cup champions.

Rugby.title: Where does Cheslin Kolbe rank in the elite goalkicking wingers' club?
Rugby.summary: Cheslin Kolbe has been perfect from the kicking tee during Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series with New Zealand, nailing four from four in the first Test and seven from seven in the second
Rugby.body:
Cheslin Kolbe has been perfect from the kicking tee during Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series with New Zealand, nailing four from four in the first Test and seven from seven in the second. Not bad for a player who’d only been a bit-part Test goalkicker up until then.

Due to the presence of Handrè Pollard and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu in the team, Kolbe did not take a single shot at goal in 2024 and 2025, and was only called upon seven times during the southern hemisphere section of this year’s Nations Championship (succeeding with five kicks). That said, he has found his rhythm with his club Suntory Sungoliath in Japan’s Rugby League One, finishing this season as top points scorer

Rugby.title: 'The All Blacks are asking South Africa all the questions that matter'
Rugby.summary: The world champions maintain a vice-like grip on the set-piece, but New Zealand are hurting them in different ways as the Greatest Rivalry series hots up.
Rugby.body:
A fisherman always spots another fisherman from afar. Giants in any field of human endeavour usually share the same competitive instincts and goals, but they rarely occupy the same space. There may be an unspoken recognition of the same traits and ambitions, an imperceptible tip of the hat from one bank to the other, but the river moves on swiftly and the focus returns, inevitably, to the float bobbing on the water. The next catch.

The two biggest pescadores of either era in rugby, amateur or professional, have been locked in silent combat for 105 years, with the just the occasional silent nod to the accomplishments of the other punctuating the torrential surge of the greatest rivalry. There have been seven prize World Cup catches between the two, with the last tussle between the twin titans decided by one single point in Paris.

Rugby.summary: Matías Moroni will have to wait until at least November to become the seventh player to win 100 caps for Argentina after being ruled out of Saturday's Test against Australia in Mendoza.
Rugby.body:
Matías Moroni will have to wait until at least November to become the seventh player to win 100 caps for Argentina after being ruled out of Saturday’s Test against Australia in Mendoza.

The outside back suffered a facial injury when coming off the bench to win his 99th cap in Saturday’s 27-21 loss to the Wallabies in Jujuy. Moroni replaced inside-centre Faustino Sanchez Valarolo in the final quarter and made six tackles and a couple of carries during his time on the pitch.

Rugby.title: England trio to make Sale Sharks debut in PREM Rugby Cup
Rugby.summary: Sale have gone full bore in their selection, handing debuts to England internationals Courtney Lawes, Joe Marchant and Alex Lozowski.
Rugby.body:
Sale Sharks boss Alex Sanderson has done ‘a Rassie Erasmus’ and gone early in naming his team for Sunday’s PREM Rugby Cup opener at home to Bath. While some clubs will treat the first batch of Cup games as a chance to give fringe players a run out, Sale have gone full bore in their selection, handing debuts to England internationals Courtney Lawes, Joe Marchant and Alex Lozowski.

Loose forward Lawes and centre/wing Marchant were big-name signings from France, while fly-half/centre Lozowski returns north having made a name for himself at Leeds before enjoying a stellar career at Wasps and then Saracens.

Rugby.title: Victor Matfield: 'He showed why he's probably the best Springbok of all time'
Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has hailed Eben Etzebeth as “probably the best Springbok of all time” after the veteran lock produced a towering response to the pressure surrounding his form in Saturday’s series-levelling 33-26 victory over the All Blacks in Cape Town.
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has hailed Eben Etzebeth as “probably the best Springbok of all time” after the veteran lock produced a towering response to the pressure surrounding his form in Saturday’s series-levelling 33-26 victory over the All Blacks in Cape Town.

The 34-year-old racked up a match-leading 18 tackles, two of which were dominant, as the world champions levelled the series with the All Blacks, but perhaps his work at the lineout was his most decisive contribution, as he terrorised the visitors’ throw at the front of the lineout.

Rugby.title: Losing Gloucester captaincy was 'brutal'
Rugby.summary: Gloucester's Lewis Ludlow on losing the captaincy last season, his two England caps, and chasing a record in his upcoming testimonial season.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester flanker Lewis Ludlow says it was "brutal" to lose the club captaincy last August and he would "take it back tomorrow" if offered. Ludlow has played more than 250 games for the Cherry and Whites and his time as skipper between 2020 and 2025 makes him the longest-serving captain in the club's history.

However, the 31-year-old was replaced by Tomos Williams in the role for the 2025-26 season, although the Welshman signed for Saracens this summer. "It was brutal," Ludlow told BBC Radio Gloucestershire about being told he was no longer captain.

Rugby.title: Pouri Rakete-Stones: Newcastle's Maori strongman with Red Bull flair and England ambitions
Rugby.summary: The former Hurricane is English-qualified, and eager to make a splash as Red Bull's fascinating overhaul of Newcastle takes shape.
Rugby.body:
In Te reo Maori, the word ‘Pouri’ tends to carry a solemn resonance. It often conveys a sense of sorrow or sadness; the echo of some grave event etched in community lore. In the Rakete-Stones family, it bears no such gloom. Certainly, the colourful and rambunctious prop who has signed up to join Newcastle’s Red Bull revolution is nothing like the sincere translation of his moniker.

Two recent Pouris came before the straggly-haired strongman from Napier. His father, Pouri senior, and his great-uncle, a redoubtable Maori who in later life, has retreated to the wilderness of New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Why Peter Lakai could be the All Blacks' ace up the sleeve for the third Test
Rugby.summary: Blindside flanker is one position Dave Rennie and the selectors have continually tinkered with while being steadfast on Savea at No.8 and Luke Jacobson at openside.
Rugby.body:
Blindside flanker is one position Dave Rennie and the selectors have continually tinkered with while being steadfast on Savea at No.8 and Luke Jacobson at openside. Peter Lakai had the first crack against France, before Wallace Sititi against Italy, and Tupou Vaa’i against Ireland. Simon Parker came into the starting line-up for his first game of the year in the second Test as Tupou Vaa’i moved back to lock.

Vaa’i had less impact than in the first Test, crucially coughing up a kick restart that led to a cheap three points for the Springboks. The lineout calls were also off, with the All Blacks attempting to throw to the middle and back too much, which were disrupted by Eben Etzebeth and Pieter-Steph du Toit. If the Boks didn’t pinch it, they often knocked it down, creating loose ball.

Rugby.title: All Blacks need to knock the front door down first
Rugby.summary: If there’s an area of concern for me, it’s in the All Blacks’ desperation to go around the Springboks. To shovel the ball across, no matter what pressure that puts on a teammate.
Rugby.body:
If that’s the standard, the All Blacks aren’t far off it. I’m not remotely discouraged by New Zealand’s 33-26 loss to South Africa in Cape Town. Yes, the lineout is under pressure and, of course, you’d like the All Blacks to be better at catching high balls. But I feared the Springboks could dish out a hiding in this match and they didn’t.

As I’ve indicated many times, this is a development tour for the All Blacks. It’s about exposing players such as Ruben Love and seeing how they cope. This is a team that’s rebuilding. The past standards of excellence don’t apply here, because of how far the All Blacks have fallen in recent times.

Rugby.title: Jason Ryan weighs in on Boks' late changes and Rassie's 'friendly fire' outburst
Rugby.summary: The scrum has been a dramatic feature of the Greatest Rivalry tour on numerous fronts, with Saturday evening's Cape Town Test adding yet another twist in the tale.
Rugby.body:
The scrum has been a dramatic feature of the Greatest Rivalry tour on numerous fronts, with Saturday evening’s Cape Town Test adding yet another twist in the tale. The game started with a selection curveball from Rassie Erasmus, who swapped his starting front row with his bench unit at the last minute. The coach later explained the move as a response to the conditions, which were drier than what was forecast earlier in the week.

After the game ended, Erasmus took exception to his All Blacks counterpart Dave Rennie expressing further concern over South Africa’s scrum tactics, accusing the hosts of making a late side-step before setting the scrum to overload the Kiwi tighthead props.

Rugby.title: SANZAAR team of the week: Springboks lead combined XV
Rugby.summary: Test Rugby at it's finest. Test two of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series and the opening exchange in the Flight Centre series between Argentina and Australia offered a contrasting set of fixtures.
Rugby.body:
Test rugby at its finest. That is what rugby fans were treated to on Saturday’s bumper back-to-back set of contrasting Southern Hemisphere series. In Cape Town, Rassie Erasmus’s world champions held the All Blacks at arm’s length without ever looking entirely home and dry to level Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Series at one a piece. To their credit, Dave Rennie’s side all but nullified the Springbok set-piece, despite ultimately falling short of landing what would have been a near-knockout blow in the series.

The legality of the Springbok scrum dominated the post-match exchanges between the two coaches, with Rennie’s pre-match messaging appearing to filter through to the officials.

Rugby.title: What Rassie’s risky business says about the Springboks
Rugby.summary: An Airlink Embraer E195 jet has no business skimming the roof of a sports stadium. Nor does a rugby coach have much business changing his team less...
Rugby.body:
An Airlink Embraer E195 jet has no business skimming the roof of a sports stadium. Nor does a rugby coach have much business changing his team less than 48 hours before kick-off, let alone replacing an entire front row an hour before the opening whistle. Yet both things happened in Cape Town.

South Africans do things differently when the stakes rise. Risk is not always a red line. Sometimes it is an invitation to create something special. The planes passed perilously close to the stadium. Rassie Erasmus’s side then staged a narrow escape of their own, absorbing an All Blacks comeback before holding on for a seven-point victory that kept the series alive. In South African rugby, the result is often its own absolution.

Rugby.summary: The Springboks hung on for a 33-26 win over the All Blacks to level the Greatest Rivalry series 1-all heading into the third Test at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

Rugby.summary: All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea says the team expected the early Springboks onslaught they received, revealing they trained all week on how to get back momentum.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea says the team expected the early Springboks onslaught they received, revealing they trained all week on how to get back momentum. Right from the first exit the Springboks went into a strong maul, then played their powerful forwards around the corner off Cobus Reinach until the halfback spotted an opportunity for Jesse Kriel to crash over a little bit wider.

The home side were up 7-0 after just two minutes, something that Tupaea says didn’t phase the All Blacks with a lot of belief in their own game. “It was something we expected. Just had to reset and go again. Obviously, nail the kick off and then get into our set piece. If I remember right, we parked up down there for a little bit after that. So yeah, took some positives from it, I guess,” Tupaea told media post-game.

Rugby.body:

Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has fired back at his All Blacks counterpart Dave Rennie for accusing his side of walking around in the scrum. The reaction came about during South Africa’s post-match press conference in Cape Town, following a tense 33-26 win for the home team in the second Test of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series. The result left the four-Test series even at one win apiece.

Moments earlier, at the All Blacks press conference, Rennie had shared his initial thoughts on the scrum contest and how it was refereed by Angus Gardner. “The scrums were better tonight,” he said. “I think Angus was pretty strong around setting a mark and trying to keep the hookers in the same spacing.

Rugby.title: Springboks hold firm against All Blacks fightback to level series
Rugby.summary: Not only did they lift their own performance, the Springboks forced Dave Rennie's side to make countless unforced errors, and make uncharacteristic kicks that handed possession back to the home side.
Rugby.body:
Staring down the barrel of trailing 2-0 in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks bounced back at DHL Stadium in Cape Town to level the four-Test series. The Springboks were always going to bite back fiercely, doing so in a way only the back-to-back Rugby World Cup winners could. The home side were dominant from the get-go, bursting out of the blocks to stun the All Blacks in the opening quarter. The visitors, who claimed a famous victory at Ellis Park in the first Test, struggled for large parts of the contest until the final 15 minutes, where Dave Rennie’s men battled back.

It was brutal by the Springboks. Not only did they lift their own performance, but the Springboks forced Dave Rennie’s side to make countless unforced errors and uncharacteristic kicks that handed possession back to the home side.

Tennis.body:
For the fourth time in five majors, there will be no British interest in the second week when the US Open moves into the latter stages. Underwhelming performances at this year's Australian Open, French Open and Wimbledon led to a series of inquests into what was going wrong.

I always think there's things that British tennis could do better. So yes, definitely," said British women's number three Francesca Jones.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu’s US Open triumph five years on, told by her opponents
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu’s US Open triumph five years on, told by her opponents The i Paper
Tennis.body:
FLUSHING MEADOWS — “Is it really five years?” says one player incredulously when I ask them what they were doing the night Emma Raducanu won the US Open. For many of us, it feels like yesterday. Raducanu’s run from qualifying to the title, never achieved at a grand slam before or since, has shaped the last five years in British tennis like few three-week periods ever have. She became and remains this country’s biggest star in women’s tennis, her every match, interview, coaching change and practice session closely followed and scrutinised.

It is typical of the rocky road Raducanu, now 23, has ridden since becoming US Open champion that she is not even here in New York to look back at the half-decade that has passed. The Big Apple has not been a happy hunting ground in that time either: she has won just two matches at this tournament since she won it.

Even though the superstar siblings - aged 44 and 46 - lost on their highly anticipated Grand Slam return, their performance in a narrow defeat by 14th seeds Chan Hao-ching and Maya Joint led to an entertaining night in New York.

Tennis.title: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka complains of cannabis smell during win over Kamilla Rakhimova to reach fourth round
Tennis.summary: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka complains of cannabis smell during win over Kamilla Rakhimova to reach fourth round Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka complained to the umpire about a strong smell of cannabis that was present duing her third-round win over Kamilla Rakhimova at the US Open. The world No 1 came through in straight sets, beating her unseeded opponent 6-3 6-4 on Louis Armstrong Stadium, but after racing into a 3-0 lead in the opening set, Sabalenka complained to umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore at the first changeover.

"I was like, 'Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around the tennis courts'," Sabalenka told reporters afterwards. "It's a bit tricky to handle that smell while you're trying to compete at your best."

Tennis.title: 'It's so strong'
Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka briefly halts her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova because of the smell of cannabis before going on to reach the fourth round.
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka briefly halted her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova because of a strong smell of cannabis before cruising into the fourth round in New York. Top seed Sabalenka raised the issue after going 3-0 up in the first set against Uzbekistan's Rakhimova, telling umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore that "someone is smoking weed".

The Belarusian asked the umpire to intervene "because it's so strong". Asderaki-Moore spoke to an official on her radio and made a smoking gesture to someone behind her, before play continued.

Aryna Sabalenka came through a tough test against Kamilla Rakhimova - particularly in the second set - to reach the fourth round of the US Open. The two-time defending champion in New York started superbly, storming into a 3-0 lead in the opening set as she didn't miss a single first serve until the seventh game of the match, in which Rakhimova would three times take her to deuce.

Tennis.title: 100 influencers invited to US Open spark debate on 'tennis etiquette'
Tennis.summary: The behaviour of influencers and content creators has become a major talking point at this year's US Open amid incidents of matches being disrupted.
Tennis.body:
When it comes to etiquette in tennis, there are a fair few unwritten rules. Apologising after winning a point from a net cord. Honesty around line calls, double bounces and double-hits. Post-match handshakes.

As for the spectators, it is common courtesy not to disturb the players during points. Around 100 influencers and content creators have been granted accreditation for the tournament in New York - double the amount from last year.

Tennis.title: Zverev battles through after enduring another 2am finish
Tennis.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev endures another gruelling five-set US Open match as he overcomes Quentin Halys at 02:15 local time to reach the third round.
Tennis.body:
Top seed Alexander Zverev endured another gruelling five-set US Open match as he overcame Quentin Halys at 02:15 local time to reach the third round. French Open champion Zverev is one of the favourites for the title, with world number one Jannik Sinner missing with injury and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz working his way back to fitness.

However, the German was taken to five sets in his first match and his level fluctuated wildly against world number 52 Halys on a humid evening in New York. An exhausted Zverev raised his arms aloft after completing a 6-4 4-6 7-6 (7-3) 6-7 (3-7) 6-3 win in four hours and 33 minutes.

Tennis.title: 'Battle-tested' Gauff reaches US Open third round
Tennis.summary: A "battle-tested" Coco Gauff shows grit to keep her bid for a second US Open title alive with victory over Paula Badosa in the second round.
Tennis.body:
A "battle-tested" Coco Gauff showed grit to keep her bid for a second US Open title alive with victory over Paula Badosa in the second round. Fourth seed Gauff had lost her past two matches against Spanish former world number two Badosa, but showed impressive composure in a tough encounter at Flushing Meadows in New York.

American Gauff was twice a break up in the second set and served for the match at 6-5, only to put a volley into the net to send it to a tie-break. After a quick yell of "why?" towards her team, Gauff reset and was solid to close out victory on a second match point.

Tennis.title: Nick Kyrgios: Former Wimbledon finalist accepts one-month suspension after positive cocaine test
Tennis.summary: Nick Kyrgios: Former Wimbledon finalist accepts one-month suspension after positive cocaine test Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Nick Kyrgios has accepted and served a reduced, one-month suspension under anti-doping rules after testing positive for cocaine at an ATP Tour event in Mallorca. Kyrgios, who had been provisionally suspended since August 4, had entered into a treatment programme approved by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) to reduce the three-month default suspension under WADA rules.

The Australian gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June which tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine. - Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱
