Tennis.title: Kyrgios given one-month ban for positive cocaine test
Tennis.summary: Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine.
Tennis.body:
Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine. The Australian, 31, was provisionally suspended on 4 August after a sample he submitted during the Mallorca Open in June was found to contain benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Kyrgios told investigators from the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) that he used cocaine at a nightclub in Magaluf in the early hours of 20 June. He played his first-round match at the Mallorca tournament two days later, losing in straight sets to compatriot Adam Walton.

Tennis.title: US Open: Naomi Osaka urges social media influencers in attendance to respect tennis 'etiquette' after second-round win
Tennis.summary: US Open: Naomi Osaka urges social media influencers in attendance to respect tennis 'etiquette' after second-round win Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Naomi Osaka urged the growing number of social media influencers at the US Open to respect the sport's "etiquette" following her second-round win over Katerina Siniakova. The issue has become a talking point at the tournament following Osaka's opening win over Anastasia Zakharova on Monday, in which viral videos have since surfaced of some influencers not paying attention to the tennis.

After overcoming a mid-match wobble to beat Katerina Siniakova 6-2 5-7 6-1 and reach the third round in New York, Osaka said on the issue: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.

Tennis.title: US Open: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in 'impossible' tennis schedule after more than four months out with a wrist injury
Tennis.summary: US Open: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in 'impossible' tennis schedule after more than four months out with a wrist injury Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz has taken a swipe at the hectic tennis calendar and said he will skip tournaments from now on. The Spaniard, who returned to action after a lengthy layoff due to a wrist injury sustained in April to defend his US Open title, said the demands of the schedule made it impossible for players to compete in every major event without risking burnout.

The Spaniard pointed to the absences of other top stars as evidence that the schedule is too demanding and will keep causing injuries. - Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱

Tennis.title: Alcaraz 'stays calm' in US Open fightback
Tennis.summary: Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz fights back from a set down to reach the US Open third round on his injury comeback.
Tennis.body:
Defending champion Carlos Alcaraz avoided the prospect of an early US Open exit by fighting back from a set down against Portugal's Jaime Faria. Alcaraz, 23, needed time to find his rhythm in the second-round contest as he continues to make his comeback from a long-term wrist injury.

But the Spanish second seed asserted his authority to win 4-6 6-0 6-3 6-2 against world number 72 Faria in the New York night session. Alcaraz fighting off two break points in the first game of the second set proved to be pivotal.

Tennis.body:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka earned one of the quickest Grand Slam wins of her career with a 53-minute pummelling of US Open debutant Polina Iatcenko in the second round.

However, the world number one did not look entirely happy even as she swept aside Iatcenko - then had a spiky exchange with a reporter in her post-match news conference. Sabalenka took umbrage with what she perceived to be a suggestion from a reporter that she had been attending "lots of parties" in the build-up to the US Open.

Tennis.title: US Open: Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar involved in testy exchange with journalist following shock exit at Flushing Meadows
Tennis.summary: US Open: Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar involved in testy exchange with journalist following shock exit at Flushing Meadows Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Spanish wonderkid Rafael Jodar was involved in a testy exchange with a journalist following his stunning exit to Chinese lucky loser Bu Yunchaokete at the US Open on Wednesday.

Jodar was tripped up at the first hurdle of his maiden campaign in New York, as the Spanish 12th seed failed to find his rhythm and fell 6-2 6-1 6-1 to Bu. Back at the site of his junior triumph two years ago, 19-year-old Jodar looked unusually out of sorts after his first-round clash was delayed by a day due to rain, with a flurry of unforced errors in defeat.

British number one Katie Boulter endured a "bad day at the office" as she won just one game in a 58-minute demolition by Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova in the US Open second round.

The match, originally scheduled to be played on one of the outer courts, was moved to the 14,000-capacity Louis Armstrong Stadium after heavy rain in New York. But fans who had counted themselves lucky to have gained a third match on their day session ticket may have been left feeling short-changed, as Boulter fell to a swift 6-1 6-0 defeat by the Czech seventh seed.

Tennis.title: What is the US Open prize money per round?
Tennis.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team look at the breakdown of a record-breaking prize fund at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
It's a record-breaking year for prize money at the US Open. The total prize money available to players is $108m (£80m), which is 20% more than the 2025 tournament - making it not just the largest-ever US Open prize pot, but the largest in Grand Slam history.

For comparison, the prize fund for Wimbledon this year was £64.2m. Of the US Open prize fund, $2m (£1.47m) goes towards a 'player support programme' after calls from players for athlete welfare across the Grand Slams, which the US Open says is "designed to complement existing end-of-career pension funds" and "will bring a range of benefits for mid-career life events and retirement transitions".

Tennis.title: Monfils wins on 40th birthday as Zverev celebrates at 2am
Tennis.summary: French veteran Gael Monfils is treated to a rendition of Happy Birthday by the US Open crowd as he becomes the oldest man to win a match there since 1992.
Tennis.body:
Most people celebrate their 40th birthday with a slap-up meal or a surprise party. Gael Monfils, the maverick Frenchman who always knows how to have fun on the court, marked his milestone by winning a Grand Slam match at the US Open.

Playing in the final major of his career, Monfils ensured he had a unforgettable night with a 2-6 6-1 6-2 6-0 victory over Paraguayan opponent Adolfo Daniel Vallejo. The former world number six is the oldest man to win a US Open main-draw match since Jimmy Connors - who also won on his 40th birthday in 1992.

Tennis.title: Gauff's flaw forgotten on winning US Open return
Tennis.summary: At last year's US Open, Coco Gauff's serve left her practising in the rain and crying on court - now it is a potent weapon.
Tennis.body:
The sight of a forlorn Coco Gauff hitting serves in the rain on the US Open practice courts became the defining image of her struggles last year. The serving yips were undermining the two-time major champion's talent. Staying out in the persistent drizzle was a sign of how desperate she had become to iron out the major flaw in her game.

Twelve months on, the 22-year-old American has returned to the US Open with a rejuvenated service game - and it was the bedrock of her 6-3 6-4 win over Turkey's Zeynep Sonmez in the New York first round on Tuesday.

Tennis.summary: After Novak Djokovic's latest bid for a historic 25th major title ends in tears in New York, where does the most decorated men's player of the Open era go from here?
Tennis.body:
Be warned: Novak Djokovic has made a fool of those who have doubted him before. Some questioned if the Serb would challenge for the sport's top honours again after he dropped out of the world's top 20 amid a two-year major title drought in 2018.

Djokovic proceeded to win four of the following five Grand Slams, doubling his tally of majors with 12 across the next six years. But three years have now passed since he landed his men's record 24th major title at the US Open.

Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka felt the love at the US Open after being given an emotional send-off following the final Grand Slam match of his career. The 41-year-old Swiss is retiring at the end of the season and looked close to tears as he received a rapturous reception after a straight-set defeat by Italy's Matteo Berrettini.

Wawrinka, who won the US Open in 2016, was initially overlooked by tournament organisers for a wildcard, but was given a last-minute reprieve following American recipient Patrick Kypson's withdrawal.

Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

After a 139-day wait, Carlos Alcaraz is back to winning ways on the singles court. The seven-time major winner walked on to Arthur Ashe Stadium on Monday to begin his US Open title defence after spending just over four months on the sidelines with a wrist injury.

Tennis.title: US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York?
Tennis.summary: US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina. Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina. Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006.

Tennis.title: Midnight matches and money disputes
Tennis.summary: BBC Sport explores the ongoing dispute over scheduling issues and late-night finishes at tennis' Grand Slam events.
Tennis.body:
When Venus Williams was awarded a wildcard for the women's singles at the US Open, she was chosen for a primetime match slot in the first round - Sunday night, on Arthur Ashe, against compatriot Sofia Kenin in front of a home crowd for possibly the final time as a solo player.

But Williams and Kenin did not end up playing on Sunday. Instead they stepped on to court just after midnight on Monday, with Kenin completing a win in straight sets shortly after the clock struck 2am local time in New York.

Tennis.title: From playing Serena Williams on screen to following in her footsteps
Tennis.summary: Having played a young Serena Williams on the big screen, teenager Thea Frodin is ready to follow in the American great's footsteps at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
Thea Frodin once played a young Serena Williams on the big screen. Now, the teenager is ready to follow in the American great's footsteps at the US Open. Five years ago, Frodin was chosen as a tennis-playing body double for the actress cast as her childhood idol in the Oscar-nominated film 'King Richard'.

That involved the then 12-year-old American working alongside actor Will Smith as he portrayed Richard Williams, the father of sisters Serena and Venus. "Being able to play the role of somebody that I looked up to for my whole life was super special," Frodin told the WTA website., external

Tennis.title: US Open: Novak Djokovic loses to Mariano Navone in longest first round match of his career in Grand Slams
Tennis.summary: US Open: Novak Djokovic loses to Mariano Navone in longest first round match of his career in Grand Slams Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic fell at the first hurdle as his tilt at a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam came to a shocking end to Argentine Mariano Navone in a five-set marathon at the US Open.

The 39-year-old went down 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 to the world No 49 in a match that lasted four hours and 36 minutes. It was the longest opening match of a Grand Slam in Djokovic's career and the earliest exit at a major since the 2006 Australian Open.

Tennis.title: Djokovic in tears during US Open first-round exit

Tennis.body:
Novak Djokovic broke down in tears during a US Open first-round defeat by Argentina's Mariano Navone which provided further evidence age is fast catching up with the 39-year-old great.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion was overcome by emotion in the deciding set of a dramatic match where he struggled physically throughout and had to vomit into a towel bin. Djokovic, seeded fourth, showed the fight for which he has always been renowned before succumbing to a 7-6 (7-5) 5-7 4-6 6-2 6-1 loss in a humid New York.

Tennis.title: GB's Samuel earns first win at a Grand Slam
Tennis.summary: British qualifier Toby Samuel breaks more new ground with a dominant victory over Tomas Machac on his US Open debut.
Tennis.body:
British qualifier Toby Samuel broke more new ground with a dominant victory over Tomas Machac on his US Open main-draw debut. The 23-year-old came from a set down in each of his three qualifying matches in New York this week to guarantee a third Grand Slam appearance of the year.

However, he had no such issues against former world number 20 Machac, wrapping up a 6-2 6-3 6-2 victory in just over 90 minutes to register his first win at a Grand Slam. "It means everything to me. It's what I dreamt of as a kid watching these big tournaments," Samuel told BBC Radio 5 Live.

Tennis.title: Tearful Federer inducted into Hall of Fame
Tennis.summary: Roger Federer says being inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame is "one of the greatest honours" of his life.
Tennis.body:
Roger Federer has been inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame, describing the moment as "one of the greatest honours" of his life. The 20-time Grand Slam singles champion, who retired in 2022, was tearful at the ceremony in Newport, Rhode Island, as he reflected on his glittering career in front of tennis greats including Billie Jean King and John McEnroe.

After make his debut in 1998 at the age of 16, Federer won a men's-record eight Wimbledon titles, six Australian Open crowns, five US Opens and one French Open. "This is one of the greatest honours of my life," Federer, 45, said.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu won the US Open five years ago. Can she ever return to those heights?
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu won the US Open five years ago. Can she ever return to those heights? The Herald
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu winning the US Open feels like both a recent memory, and like it happened a lifetime ago. The 2026 US Open begins in New York today and marks five years since the young Brit made that remarkable run to the title at Flushing Meadows.

So much has happened since Raducanu made all different types of history in 2021, though, and the past five years have panned out in a way few would have predicted as she held the trophy aloft - for all the wrong reasons.

Tennis.body:
All was bright in Aryna Sabalenka's world when she completed a rare 'Sunshine Double' earlier this season. Becoming only the fifth woman to win the Indian Wells and Miami titles back-to-back, Sabalenka emphasised her position as the dominant player on the WTA Tour and created a 3,000-point lead at the top of the world rankings.

But a difficult period quickly followed - seemingly out of nowhere - leaving the 28-year-old Belarusian clinging on to her position going into the US Open, which starts on Sunday.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper x Axel Arigato Reveal 'Midnight' Sneakers Collaboration
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper x Axel Arigato Reveal 'Midnight' Sneakers Collaboration Yahoo
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper and Axel Arigato have unveiled "Midnight," the final chapter in their trilogy of sneaker collaborations. Ahead of the US Open, the UK tennis star is completing the trilogy of collaborations with "Midnight," a black take on the Dice silhouette with teal accents. Following "Dusk" and "Rise," the new pair of sneakers celebrates the institution of night sessions. The timing of its release, on Wednesday (Aug. 26), coincides with the start of the US Open, which became the first Grand Slam to play under floodlights in 1975.

"Everything about New York feels bigger at night," said Jack Draper of the final sneaker collaboration in the trilogy. "The city, the noise, those late sessions—it's got that Gotham energy I've always loved. Midnight is the shoe for that: dark, sharp, made for after hours. It felt like the only way to finish the trilogy."

Golf.title: LIV Golf Embarrassment Continues at DP World Tour Q-School
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Embarrassment Continues at DP World Tour Q-School Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
As LIV Golf's future remains uncertain, professional golfer Peter Uihlein entered to compete in the DP World Tour Q-School, but he failed to show up to his third round tee-time. He started the event poorly, shooting a 74 and a 73 in the first two rounds respectively. When he was not at the tee on Friday, the event disqualified him off the leaderboard. Prior to his disqualification, he stood at 66th place and required a 19th place finish at least to advance further in the competition.

Many of those involved with LIV Golf like Uihlein are still awaiting news about their future. They need to plan contingencies unless LIV Golf 2.0, the next stage of the startup, fails to launch. Fellow LIV Golfers Luis Masaveu and Jose Luis Ballester are also participating in the event to qualify for DP World Tour status.

Golf.title: 2026's winning PGA Tour irons prove 1 thing: Blades still rule
Golf.summary: Nearly half of the 2026 PGA Tour FedEx Cup events were won by players with blade irons. Check out the full list of the winningest irons. The post 2026’s winning PGA Tour irons prove 1 thing: Blades still rule appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Remember at the beginning of the season when Rory McIlroy switched into a set of cavity-back irons, and more pros were switching out of blades seemingly every week? Not only did McIlroy switch back to his TaylorMade RORS Proto blades before his season debut at Pebble Beach and ultimately used them to win his second-straight Masters, the first five events of the PGA Tour season were also won by blade players.

Ultimately, blade players won 17 of the FedEx Cup regular season’s 37 events, a not-so-insignificant share. Players still value the precision and control offered by muscle back irons en masse on the PGA Tour.

Ultimately, blade players won 17 of the FedEx Cup regular season’s 37 events, a not-so-insignificant share. Players still value the precision and control offered by muscle back irons en masse on the PGA Tour.

Golf.body:
Peter Uihlein, who has played in LIV Golf tournaments since 2023, played two rounds at a DP World Tour first-stage qualifying school event this week and was disqualified. Uihlein’s DQ came at Huddersfield Golf Club in Huddersfield, England. He opened with rounds of four-over 74 and three-over 73, then was booted from the event after he failed to show for his third round, Bunkered’s Josh Lees reported.

The disqualification comes as the future of LIV Golf remains unclear. Two weeks ago, the league finished its fifth season of play, but it’s now trying to manage the loss of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund. LIV CEO Scott O’Neil has said the league has received a signed term sheet with a lead investor, but has yet to name it, saying there’s “a very compressed timeline to get the deal done.”

Golf.title: New Zealand has become the ultimate golf dream trip. Here's why
Golf.summary: New Zealand has more golf courses per capita than any country other than Scotland, in a setting of unrivaled serenity and beauty. The post New Zealand has become the ultimate golf dream trip. Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
On the world clock, New Zealand is well ahead of the United States. But North American golfers have been catching up. They’ve come to recognize the country as a must-visit, magnetic for the quality and diversity of its courses, the beauty of its landscapes and the welcoming spirit of its people.

That awareness wasn’t born overnight. It began stirring decades ago with the opening of Kauri Cliffs and Cape Kidnappers, luxurious resorts whose seaside layouts, stunning scenery and A-list accommodations remain emblems of New Zealand’s coastal splendor. The more recent arrival of marquee properties like Tara Iti and Te Arai — which combined to deliver three new courses to GOLF’s World Top 100 list — attracted next-level attention that was further magnified by the Covid golf boom. As the spotlight brightened on the North Island, it radiated outward, illuminating a golf scene of remarkable depth and range.

Golf.title: Testing the YouTube famous Takomo Irons. (Hint: They're impressive)
Golf.summary: The curiosity around Takomo irons has been loud. We wanted to find out why — and the results were very impressive The post Testing the YouTube famous Takomo Irons. (Hint: They’re impressive) appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ll just start here: I was late to the Takomo party. I knew the name. I’d seen the irons. I’d seen them all over YouTube and Instagram. I knew Takomo was one of those direct-to-consumer brands that had managed to build a pretty serious following without playing by the traditional golf-equipment rulebook. But knowing about something and actually hitting it are two very different things. There are plenty of golf clubs I’ve looked at, read about and formed an opinion on before ever putting one behind a ball. Then you actually hit them and realize the opinion you had was based on absolutely nothing. Which, to be fair, is kind of how the internet works.

So when I finally got some time with the Takomo irons, I went into it with one question: What’s the catch? Because golf equipment has conditioned us to think that way. If an iron looks premium, feels premium and performs like the stuff hanging on the wall at your local golf shop, we generally expect the price tag to reflect it. That’s just how this has worked for a long time. Good golf equipment costs good golf-equipment money.

Golf.title: Stomach issues again hit Walker Cup. And alternate is on ‘standby’
Golf.summary: Stomach issues again hit the Walker Cup, an amateur event played this year at Lahinch Golf Club in Ireland. And an alternate is on “standby.” The post Stomach issues again hit Walker Cup. And alternate is on ‘standby’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The U.S. Walker Cup team is now “bouncing around,” its captain, Nathan Smith, says. And his players’ stomachs, it appears, have mostly stopped rumbling. On Thursday, two days before this weekend’s amateur event, that features a 10-man American team meeting a 10-man Great Britain and Ireland team at Ireland’s Lahinch Golf Club, Golf Channel’s Brentley Romine reported that multiple Americans were fighting “stomach issues.” Ethan Feng and William Jennings, Romine said, did not practice on Thursday, and three players didn’t attend that night’s banquet.

At a Friday press conference, though, Smith said every player would be ready for Saturday, though the Americans’ first alternate, Max Herendeen, has been contacted and is on “standby” — though he’s not on site.

Golf.title: A muni made me wait 30 mins on an empty course. Was that fair?
Golf.summary: In its quest to enforce the rules, the pro shop at a California muni lost sight of the bigger picture and alienated a customer. The post A muni made me wait 30 mins on an empty course. Was that fair? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I recently made a tee time at my local muni for the first twilight spot of the afternoon. I arrived at the course about 35 minutes early, paid my green fee and was on the putting green when I noticed that the 1st hole was wide open. I spoke to the starter, who told me I could go. But as I stepped up to the tee, the woman who’d checked me in burst from the pro shop and yelled at me to stop. Because I’d paid the discounted twilight rate, she said, I’d have to wait until twilight officially began. Never mind that there were no groups waiting to tee off. I looked plaintively at the starter, who shrugged. He was outranked. I tried to reason with the pro shop staffer, but she insisted that I couldn’t start my round. And so I waited for another 30 minutes, with the course empty in front of me and no other golfers teeing off.

To say that I was irritated is an understatement. I’m a regular at the course and the staffer’s decision struck me as spiteful and small-minded. Was I wrong to be annoyed? As we all know, rules are rules, and they’re meant to be followed. But sometimes they can also be harmlessly broken. Let’s say you’re playing a friendly match with a pal at a poorly conditioned course, and his ball lands in a footprint in the bunker. When he asks if he can move his ball without penalty, you say sure. Have you violated the letter of the law? Technically, yes. Have you made a reasonable decision? Also, yes. On the course, as off it, common sense and context should be our guides.

Golf.title: As the golf season winds down, Arccos keeps me improving
Golf.summary: I discovered a new area of golf focus on my Arccos app this month, and it's helping me understand my game beyond the clubs or the swing. The post As the golf season winds down, Arccos keeps me improving appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ve spent another month with Arccos game-tracking but this time most of my rounds were spent testing out upcoming club releases. It’s interesting to see what happens to my game when I’m not using my normal set, not to mention the new feature (or possibly one that I missed previously) that I’d love to dive into.

I’m still using the Arccos Air and the Arccos Smart Laser every time I play (as long as the course is rated) and both devices have been nothing but flawless. Now that I’ve been using the system for a good bit of time, the accuracy continues to improve and I am essentially at a point where I don’t even touch my phone or the app during my round, and everything is logged, no problem. Let’s use my August golf recap to see 1) where we’re at, 2) what clubs could land in the bag, and 3) what I still need to work on.

Within the first three minutes of the video, you’ll hear me state “yeah, well, blades are better” as Sweeney introduces our topic of the day, but writing this now four months later, a custom TaylorMade Spider Tour X has been in my bag ever since.

Golf.title: John Ashworth shares the keys to effortless on-course style

Golf.body:
For nearly five decades, there has been one universally agreed upon poster boy for effortless golf: Fred Couples. Beginning in the late ’80s, Couples’ on-course cool was buoyed by his apparel partnership with Ashworth, the laidback, SoCal brand founded by its namesake designer, John Ashworth. Player and polo were a perfect match.

Ashworth left the brand in 1997, only to return in 2024. Needless to say, when it comes to guidance for de-stressed on-course dressing, there’s only one guy for the job. Here are Ashworth’s keys for feeling effortless, because even the king of apparel cool would say that’s way more crucial than looking the part.

Golf.title: Washington D.C. is at odds over one of its beloved golf courses
Golf.summary: Is President Trump's promise for construction at a D.C. muni coming to fruition? Or will it be decided in court? The post Washington D.C. is at odds over one of its beloved golf courses appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
After months of relative quiet, the attention of President Trump’s various building projects in Washington D.C. has turned to one of the district’s municipal courses, albeit with little certainty about the administration’s official plans.

This is the increasingly popular case of East Potomac Golf Links, a 36-hole muni property in the heart of D.C. that Trump has sought to renovate into an 18-hole championship golf course. In late June, President Trump targeted Sept. 1 as the official start date for construction on the course, and while heavy machinery arrived on-site this week, that date has now passed without much proof of significant course alterations.

Golf.title: 1 answer to golf's amateur debate was on display at the U.S. Women's Mid-Am
Golf.summary: Ally Shepherd won the U.S. Women's Mid-Amateur on Thursday in New Jersey, ending a week filled with debate about golf's amateur status. The post 1 answer to golf’s amateur debate was on display at the U.S. Women’s Mid-Am appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ivy Shepherd’s putt fell on the 14th hole on Thursday at the U.S. Women’s Mid-Amateur and the tears fell soon after. It’d been a long, turbulent journey for Shepherd — one that had brought her to the heights of the collegiate amateur circuit and the doldrums of competitive golf. Now, for a few fleeting moments, it was complete.

She was a U.S. Women’s Mid-Am champion, and she was headed to the U.S. Women’s Open. “It’s awesome. It’s the longest freaking Women’s Open qualifier in the history of the world. But it’s cool,” Shepherd said. “All that is just awesome, you know, results and rewards for a long week of competitive golf for somebody who is going to end up winning it. Again, just tons of gratitude. Yeah, I feel very, very blessed.”

Golf.title: Just 3 2026 PGA Tour winners used this once-popular club type
Golf.summary: Hybrids used to dominate the PGA Tour. Now, while long irons survive as utilities, hybrids are on life support. The post Just 3 2026 PGA Tour winners used this once-popular club type appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Five years ago, hybrids were still a regular part of bags on the PGA Tour. Even Rory McIlroy was using one. Today, they’re almost nonexistent, with only three PGA Tour winners across 37 events carrying one for their victory this past FedEx Cup season.

On the PGA Tour, hybrids have been largely replaced by high-lofted fairway woods and a resurgent uptick in utility irons, thanks to advances in technology for both alternatives.

For the first time in more than half a decade, Mizuno has a true better-player cavity-back iron. The Japanese sports giant, which has always been known for producing soft-feeling forged irons, has recently shed the idea that their irons are only for better players and become one of the market leaders in players distance and game improvement irons. In their current lineup, Mizuno has at least four different irons that could be categorized as players distance.

Meanwhile, the first two offerings in the new Mizuno Pro Signature Series, the S-1 and S-3, were a compact blade and a compact shallow cavity. Irons designed for elite ball strikers, but not as much for a player who wanted just a touch of forgiveness.

Golf.title: Jon Rahm’s LIV Golf Future Faces Uncertain Cliff
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm’s LIV Golf Future Faces Uncertain Cliff Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm stands at a crossroads that could define the rest of his career. The two-time major champion's future with LIV Golf looks shaky as the league tries to secure new funding. Reports suggest the breakaway tour might not keep him. This isn't just a small contract dispute. It involves a massive $150 million sum still owed to the Spanish star. As the league restructures, the man many called their flagship player might be walking away. The situation creates a ripple effect across professional golf, leaving fans wondering where the 31-year-old will play next season.

When Rahm jumped to the rebel tour in late 2023, he signed a deal loaded with cash. Per multiple reports, he is still owed around $150 million from that multi-year contract. That figure makes his position unique and complicated. As LIV Golf fights to bring in a new lead investor, reportedly BC Partners, the league's financial math changes. His contract now looks out of bounds for the new owners. Losing such a high-profile talent would be a huge blow to the league's credibility. LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil admitted the stakes were high. To reach and complete this transaction is the sole focus of our efforts. Without the players, that becomes very difficult, O'Neil said, as reported by reports. The pressure is on to close the deal while keeping stars like Rahm happy.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf staff 'struggling to pay mortgages and bills' as bankruptcy impact laid bare AOL.com
Golf.body:
Freelance workers say they have not been paid by LIV Golf as the troubled league prepares to declare bankruptcy. LIV is widely expected to file for voluntary bankruptcy in the coming days after the termination of Saudi Arabia's financial support. The Public Investment Fund (PIF), which launched LIV in 2022 and backed it with billions of dollars, announced in April that it was withdrawing its support, and the split was completed on Sep. 1.

The league has agreed terms in principle for a rescue package worth in the region of $300 million with private equity firm BC Partners. The deal has yet to be finalized, but LIV is confident of getting it over the line. Imminent bankruptcy, though, remains likely.

Golf.body:
American golf brand Good Good has sacked two senior executives following backlash over an advert which showed a woman being pushed to the ground after reaching for a club. The company, whose YouTube channel has 2.1m subscribers, said it had parted ways with chief executive Matt Kendrick and president Joe Flannery following the release last month of the advert created for golf club manufacturer Callaway.

Good Good vice-president of brand and marketing Jeffrey Lefkovits was sacked earlier this week. Head of finance and operations at Good Good, Alex Puchala, said the dismissals on Wednesday were a "difficult day for the entire Good Good family".

Golf.title: How a Ryder Cup rules controversy kept Jason Day from the Presidents Cup

Golf.body:
When Presidents Cup rosters were finalized Tuesday, a few notable exclusions stood out. On the American side, captain Brandt Snedeker went with budding young star Jackson Koivun and Genesis Invitational winner Jacob Bridgeman over Ryder Cuppers Ben Griffin and J.J. Spaun. For the Internationals, one big name did not make Geoff Ogilvy’s squad: Jason Day.

The 2015 PGA Champion and former World No. 1 has played in five Presidents Cups and is one of the biggest names on an International side that lacks star power outside of Hideki Matsuyama and Adam Scott. But the 38-year-old Day dealt with a back injury for a big part of the 2026 season. It forced him to withdraw pre-tournament from the 3M Open and the Rocket Classic and contributed to Day missing the FedEx Cup Playoffs for the first time in 18 years.

Golf.title: Tiger Woods strikes plea deal in DUI case, has license suspended
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods reached a plea deal in a DUI case stemming from a March car accident and had his license suspended for five years. The post Tiger Woods strikes plea deal in DUI case, has license suspended appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Tiger Woods will be off the road for five years. On Wednesday morning, the 15-time major champion changed his plea in a DUI case stemming from his car accident in March and had his license suspended for five years as part of a deal to avoid jail time.

Woods was arrested in Jupiter, Fla. at the end of March on suspicion of driving under the influence after his car struck the back of a maintenance vehicle and flipped over on a one-lane road. Nobody was injured in the crash, but a short police investigation resulted in Woods failing a field sobriety test. Officers at the scene of the crash arrested Woods and charged him with DUI, and also recovered two pills inside his pocket that Woods identified as hydrocodone, a prescription opioid.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Hopes Screwing Its Own Players In Bankruptcy Will Secure Its Future
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Hopes Screwing Its Own Players In Bankruptcy Will Secure Its Future Defector
Golf.body:
LIV Golf recently sent out a mass email to mark the conclusion of its 2026 season. I imagine this was a somewhat slapdash operation given that the outfit, recently dumped by the Saudi Public Investment Fund, had to lop off the final event on its schedule, the team championship, which was scheduled for the final weekend of August, in Plymouth, Mich. Instead, the player championship and the team championship were both settled in Indianapolis, with stripped down entertainment offerings and drastically reduced player bonuses. In the week between the season's sudden conclusion and the arrival of the email, LIV Golf laid off a majority of its employees, writing in a statement to Golf Digest that the operation had "informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0" had concluded. Perhaps the exodus and confusion explain how they got the email wrong: Mine addressed me as "Dear LIV Golf Fan" and thanked me for supporting their terrible league. Not me! I've been to two LIV Golf events and both sucked mega shit.

The email encourages recipients to "stay tuned for more LIV Golf," without offering any details whatsoever about where a LIV Golf Fan might do that, or for how long. The promotion's future is very much up in the air. In the statement announcing the layoffs, a LIV Golf spokesperson insisted that whoever is left over there is still working "toward making LIV 2.0 a reality."

Golf.body:
Jon Rahm is set for a busy run on the golf course as he awaits news on LIV Golf's future, with the troubled league facing bankruptcy. Two-time major champion Rahm is believed to be the league's biggest creditor, still owed a nine-figure sum from the blockbuster contract he signed to jump ship from the PGA Tour in 2023.

The former world No. 1 has been linked with a return to the PGA Tour as LIV's future hangs in the balance, with some staff fearing that Rahm will quit regardless of whether a rescue deal funded by private equity firm BC Partners is finalized.

He pleaded not guilty the same month to misdemeanor charges of driving under the influence and refusal to submit to testing. Woods, 50, said he was seeking treatment after the incident.

To-date, the League has impacted more than one million young people’s lives through its Impact and Sustainability initiatives. Through its Game pillar, LIV Golf is actively removing historic barriers to entry and expanding access to the sport worldwide, exceeding its ambitious annual target to introduce 15,000 new youth to golf in 2026. This commitment to youth development is reflected globally through tailored regional programs and team initiatives.

The name is a nod to Lee’s on-course nickname, the Chef, which evolved from Lee’s “Let him cook” captions on social media.

Now, the PGA Tour winner and top-30 player is sporting his very own shoe. “I wanted a shoe that felt locked in and responsive when I’m swinging at full speed, but I also wanted it to look clean, premium and different from anything else out there,” Lee said in a release. “This was a true collaborative process with the PAYNTR Golf team, and we kept testing and refining the shoe until every detail felt right. The CHEF RX RS gives me the stability, comfort and traction I need to go after it while still representing my personality and style. I’m excited for golfers to experience our creation on the golf course.”

Golf.title: This driver shaft (and brand) continues to dominate the PGA Tour
Golf.summary: Fujikura didn't sweep the majors in 2026, but its Ventus lineup of shafts had more wins than any other brand. The post This driver shaft (and brand) continues to dominate the PGA Tour appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
A year after a Fujikura driver shaft swept all four major championships, they’re again at the top of the pecking order for winners on the PGA Tour. While Fujikura didn’t get the major sweep again in 2026, the company led the winning counts for driver shafts on the PGA Tour once again. Its Ventus line of shafts had more victories than any other brand’s entire catalog and the Ventus Black profile itself had as many victories as the second-place brand.

What’s also impressive is that the driver shaft market on the PGA Tour is effectively dominated by three brands, with Mitsubishi and Project X also having solid years this season.

Golf.title: LIV Golf on the verge of bankruptcy
Golf.summary: LIV Golf on the verge of bankruptcy Mundo Deportivo
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is facing a critical period. The men’s golf circuit, launched in 2022 by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, or PIF, has reportedly sought bankruptcy protection after laying off most of its workforce while continuing its search for a lead investor following the PIF’s withdrawal, according to the Financial Times.

The circuit recently sent settlement offers to current players who are owed millions of dollars in guaranteed payments extending beyond 2026. A bankruptcy filing could be submitted in federal district court in New Jersey, while the PIF is expected to provide less than $100 million in bankruptcy financing, without committing additional funds.

Golf.body:
Tour Edge continues to revamp its product line, and its latest introduction targets the short game. The company is announcing its new Exotics Milled Wedge Series featuring 17 different loft and grind combinations and a tri-sole design to give players options within the brand.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: If the group ahead is slow, can I take more than 3 minutes to find my ball?
Golf.summary: If you're waiting on the group ahead, can you use the extra time to search for your ball for more than 3 minutes? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: If the group ahead is slow, can I take more than 3 minutes to find my ball? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. Let’s say, while playing behind a slow group, I hit my ball into an area where I can’t find it in the allotted 3 minutes. If I couldn’t play my next shot anyway because they’re delaying my pace of play, can I continue to look for my ball without penalty? – Barry Nygard, via email

It’s a reasonable thought, Barry…but reasonableness isn’t the standard here. The three-minute search time is a hard deadline, regardless of whether slowpokes would have had you waiting. Once you or your caddie (or your partner or partner’s caddie in partner formats) start to search for your ball, if it’s not found within that allotted three minutes it is lost and no longer in play, and Rule 18.2b requires that you play under stroke and distance. (See also Definition of Lost.)

Golf.title: The Future Is Bright For LIV Golf’s Youngest Winner
Golf.summary: The Future Is Bright For LIV Golf’s Youngest Winner livgolf.com
Golf.body:
The swagger was there from the start. The gold chain around his neck, visible and prominent thanks to his always-unbuttoned polo. The high-crowned cap that seemed a half-size larger than everybody else’s. The cocky demeanor balanced by the megawatt smile and funny charm of a 22-year-old determined to enjoy the moment at hand.

And, of course, those huge quadriceps, apparent even when wearing long pants and certainly intimidating whenever he wore shorts, the thin fabric unable to contain the ripples on display with every tee shot. At first glance, he looked less like a golfer and more like one of those rugby props doing battle on the front line of a scrum.

Golf.title: The winningest driver of the 2026 FedEx Cup season might surprise you
Golf.summary: For the second year in a row, the winningest driver of the FedEx Cup season was a 2024 model. See the full list of winningest drivers. The post The winningest driver of the 2026 FedEx Cup season might surprise you appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Make no mistake, 2026 was a driver year. That’s reflected in the bags of this year’s PGA Tour winners. Callaway, Ping, Srixon, TaylorMade and Titleist all had drivers released this year win on the PGA Tour this season, with TaylorMade and Titleist’s 2026 models winning multiple times.

But in the end, for the third straight season, it was actually a driver released in 2024 that took the cake as the winningest driver of 2026. With a whopping eight victories, three of them by Matt Fitzpatrick, Titleist’s GT3 was the winningest driver of 2026.

Golf.title: Viktor Hovland's Tour Championship near-miss leads him to great 'philosophical question'
Golf.summary: Viktor Hovland had the Tour Championship in his grasp before Scottie Scheffler grabbed it. That near-miss has Hovland facing a big question. The post Viktor Hovland’s Tour Championship near-miss leads him to great ‘philosophical question’ appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Viktor Hovland is both a big-picture thinker and someone who is myopically focused. Such is the blessing and curse of the gifted, those given rare talent and a brain that never stops tinkering.

So after watching Scottie Scheffler run past him on Sunday at the Tour Championship, Hovland looked at the 10,000-foot view of his season, one that saw him beat Scheffler in a playoff at the Travelers and hold the 54-hole lead at East Lake. It was a season in which he contended while still searching for the feeling that has been missing since he started re-working his swing after his 2023 FedEx Cup win. Viktor Hovland is still searching for Viktor Hovland. So, in that sense, it’s positive that he can still contend with and beat the best in the world while trying to reach through smoke to grab whom he used to be. But the other part of Hovland, the one who is focused on the small details of everything, saw himself lose the first 54-hole lead of his career because he’s still not that Viktor Hovland.

Golf.title: This common swing fault could make you a better putter
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Tommy O'Brien Jr. shares how thinking about a "hook" could help you become a better putter. The post This common swing fault could make you a better putter appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Hitting better putts can be easily achieved through understanding what type of full-swing motion makes a ball roll better. Every golfer has hit a hook or a slice with their full swing, but which one makes the ball roll out more? We all know the answer: the hook. Many of the top putters throughout history illustrate this well, as almost all of them have fought a hook with their full swing at some point in their careers.

In my experience, it’s uncanny how often players employ traits of their full swing in their putting stroke. Think about the players who have struggled with putting throughout their careers. Typically, they are some of the best ball strikers in the world — players who hit a “trap cut,” allowing them to dominate the ball-striking categories while falling short on the greens.

Golf.title: 5 winners (besides Scottie Scheffler) from PGA Tour's playoffs
Golf.summary: By traditional measurements (lowest score, most victories) Scottie Scheffler won the PGA Tour's FedEx Cup Playoffs. But these guys won, too. The post 5 winners (besides Scottie Scheffler) from PGA Tour’s playoffs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Scottie Scheffler is the best golfer on the PGA Tour. That is the least interesting but most true sentence we’ll include here, but it’s worth establishing off the top; Scheffler reaffirmed his position atop the game at Sunday’s Tour Championship with a round of 66 that catapulted him past the 54-hole leaders and broke the collective spirit of every other player in contention.

Scheffler’s season had been notably strange because he finished second place five different times to five different very worthy opponents. But on Sunday he got the last laugh; for the second time in three weeks, he left all five in the dust. Jackson Koivun (who beat him at the 3M Open) was at home; his next shot at Scheffler will come in 2027. Matt Fitzpatrick (who beat him at the RBC Heritage) was well off the pace in a share of 21st. Cameron Young (who beat him at the Cadillac) was unable to summon any momentum en route to T11. Rory McIlroy (who beat him at the Masters) started too far back to challenge and finished T4. And Viktor Hovland (who beat him at the Travelers) began Sunday three shots ahead of Scheffler but finished three shots behind.

Golf.title: Presidents Cup captain's picks: Locks, bubble players and long shots

Golf.body:
The 2026 PGA Tour regular season came to an end on Sunday with Scottie Scheffler winning his second FedEx Cup title. With the regular season done and dusted, Scheffler will turn his attention to the 2026 Presidents Cup, which will be contested at Medinah Country Club in Chicago from Sept. 22-27. Scheffler was one of six players to automatically qualify for U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker’s team, along with Wyndham Clark, Sam Burns, Cameron Young, Russell Henley and Collin Morikawa. Geoff Ogilvy’s International team finished its qualification period on Sunday, with Adam Scott, Si Woo Kim, Tom Kim, Ryan Fox, Hideki Matsuyama and Min Woo Lee punching their ticket to Medinah.

The captains will announce their six remaining picks at 5 p.m. ET Tuesday on Golf Channel. But who are the picks? Let’s break down the locks, bubble players, long shots and one burning question for each team.

Golf.title: Report: LIV Golf eyes bankruptcy filing as soon as next week
Golf.summary: Report: LIV Golf eyes bankruptcy filing as soon as next week Sports Business Journal
Golf.body: LIV Golf “may file for bankruptcy protection as soon as next week” as the circuit “races to find funding for a slimmed-down version slated for 2027,” according to sources cited by the FINANCIAL TIMES. The league “in recent days has sent settlement offers to the current LIV players who are owed millions in guaranteed payouts past 2026,” with those initial offers “at just a few cents on the dollar.” For several weeks, LIV has been “negotiating a funding package” with the credit division of private capital firm BC Partners, and BC executives have “attended recent LIV tournaments in Indiana and New Jersey to make their pitch to players.” LIV’s bankruptcy filing “may be made in the federal district court of New Jersey, a venue that is known to be friendly to debtors.” BC Partners, “while conducting due diligence, is itself waiting for LIV and PIF to resolve player payments and structure the bankruptcy terms” (FINANCIAL TIMES, 8/31).

Golf.title: Rose Zhang didn't win the FM Championship but she left with the next best thing
Golf.summary: As Rose Zhang tried to play her way onto the Solheim Cup team this year, one question followed her. She answered it at the FM Championship. The post Rose Zhang didn’t win the FM Championship but she left with the next best thing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rose Zhang knew this would be a weird year for her on the course after finishing up her Stanford degree in the spring. Transitioning back to being a full-time pro was going to have its bumps, but the former Stanford star faced it with one big goal in mind.

In two previous Solheim Cup appearances, Zhang went 4-2-1 and looked to cement herself as part of the backbone of future teams along with Nelly Korda. But after stepping back from full-time competitive golf to finish her degree at Stanford, Zhang’s world-class game was rusty and she knew she needed to prove herself to coach Angela Stanford to make the 2026 team. Zhang struggled in her return to full-time LPGA play earlier this year. She missed the cut at the JM LA Eagle Championsho and the Chevron Championship. After a T9 at the Ford in March, Zhang posted just one top-12 finish in her next 10 starts. She made the cut at the four majors after the Chevron but didn’t finish better than T41. As the calendar turned to August, Zhang had one thought as she tried to prove she should be Stanford’s team that will compete in the Netherlands during the second week of September.

Golf.title: Ruoning Yin returns to winner's circle with emotional victory in Boston
Golf.summary: After two years without a victory, Ruoning Yin rejoined the winner's circle Sunday at the FM Championship. The post Ruoning Yin returns to winner’s circle with emotional victory in Boston appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
NORTON, Mass. — After two years without a victory, Ruoning Yin finally had her moment again. Yin closed out a hard-fought final round Sunday at the FM Championship with a 2-under 70, including a two-putt birdie on the par-5 18th to win by two and capture the sixth LPGA Tour title of her career.

The victory was Yin’s first since 2024 and came after a week in which she repeatedly found herself battling for the lead with Hyo Joo Kim and Sei Young Kim. She stayed patient throughout the final round, even as the leaderboard shifted, and finished the week with 24 birdies—the most of any player in the field.

Golf.title: 'Never gave up': LPGA legend's emotional goodbye week ended with a message
Golf.summary: Anna Nordqvist's competitive career ended at the FM Championship. After a finishing par, she delivered a message. The post ‘Never gave up’: LPGA legend’s emotional goodbye week ended with a message appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Anna Nordqvist has always been wired to compete. You don’t win 16 times worldwide, including three majors, and make nine Solheim Cup teams without loving the grind and the fight. So, even as the 39-year-old, who announced Wednesday that she’d be retiring from competitive golf after this week’s FM Championship, was playing the final holes of a legendary career, she could only think about one thing.

“I’m a competitor. I don’t know how the putt doesn’t go in on eight or how the putt doesn’t go in on the last hole,” Nodqvist said on Sunday after shooting a final-round even-par 72 to finish T38.

Golf.title: 5 reasons every golfer should practice hitting balls off a tee
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel explains why hitting golf balls off a tee is a great way to practice your swing. The post 5 reasons every golfer should practice hitting balls off a tee appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of my favorite training aids when I teach is the simple golf tee. There are so many ways you can use a tee to help improve your motion and provide valuable feedback. Surprisingly, golfers often think it is a penalty to have to use a tee, but I strongly believe the opposite: you can use the tee to your advantage.

Here are five reasons I believe every golfer should practice hitting balls off a tee. Once you are into a full swing, it can be a great idea to start with a low tee to get the swing going without having to worry as much about hitting the ball and then the ground. Using the tee as feedback for where you are hitting the ground is very helpful. When swinging any club other than the driver, the tee should be hit and even broken if you are swinging with enough speed. Doing this during your warm-up can build confidence and help the rest of the day go better.

Golf.title: ‘I love you, dude’: Tiger Woods honored a friend. It was both touching and telling
Golf.summary: Tiger Woods’s most recent semi-public appearance came by way of a video message he made for childhood friend Notah Begay. The post ‘I love you, dude’: Tiger Woods honored a friend. It was both touching and telling appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The other day, Holly Finchem revealed to the golf-loving world, via Global Golf Post, that her husband, Tim Finchem, has Alzheimer’s. In his 22 years as PGA Tour commissioner — the Tiger Years, essentially — Finchem was always of sound mind and body. He was always a trim and fit man. But the former—his strategic and lawyerly brain — was his bread and butter, and now a disease with no known cure has settled in it.

Holly Finchem’s forthright and powerful commentary brought to mind the last time husband and wife, married for nearly 40 years, were at the center of golf’s spotlight, on a Wednesday night in March of 2022, on the eve of the Players Championship, when Finchem was inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame. Tiger Woods was the headliner that evening — he was inducted that night, too. Finchem and Woods sat next to one another for most of the night, in the first row of a space-age auditorium of the Tour’s new headquarters, its “Global Home,” per the Tour’s own branding. Finchem wrapped up his remarks by publicly thanking Holly “for agreeing to marry me.” It was both lawyerly and moving. It was a beautiful thing to say. Beautiful and easy.

Golf.title: Adam Scott's Tour Championship contention a reminder of pro golf's constant force
Golf.summary: Adam Scott's Tour Championship contention is a reminder of pro golf's main constant force and one thing that has kept it at bay. The post Adam Scott’s Tour Championship contention a reminder of pro golf’s constant force appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Twenty years ago this November, the PGA Tour’s Tour Championship was contested in early November. It was still held at East Lake Golf Club, but it was a time before the FedEx Cup, before the professional golf world as we know it began to take shape. A time before LIV Golf was born and (maybe?) died, before Brian Rolapp arrived and worked to reshape the PGA Tour’s postseason model from the FedEx Cup to a new iteration that will begin in 2028. That week, as the PGA Tour’s 30 best players were playing in Atlanta, Tom Brady threw four interceptions in a Sunday Night Football loss to Peyton Manning and the Indianapolis Colts. Brady would go on to play 16 more seasons, win four more Super Bowls and retire in 2022.

On that Sunday in 2006 at East Lake, Adam Scott defeated Jim Furyk to win the Tour Championship. A lot has changed about golf and the world since that November in 2006. Change has been a constant force in pro golf ever since Tiger Woods arrived, forever altering the sport, and it has only accelerated over the last decade. The money grows, the sponsors and tournaments and schedules shift and the players get younger and better.

Golf.title: At FM Championship, 1 major Solheim Cup question emerged
Golf.summary: Angel Yin returned to competition for the first time in two months at the FM Championship and brought a big Solheim Cup question with her. The post At FM Championship, 1 major Solheim Cup question emerged appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
FM Championship week began with U.S. captain Angela Stanford selecting Rose Zhang, Megan Khang and Lindy Duncan as the final three members of her team to travel to the Netherlands in two weeks. But while Stanford’s roster was technically completed on Monday, one big question remained.

One that took center stage during the first two days of the FM Championship at TPC Boston. Angel Yin, who made the U.S. Solheim Cup team on points, withdrew from the third round of the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship in June and hasn’t played since. Yin told Golfweek’s Beth Ann Nichols that she had stomach and gastrointestinal problems that caused her to lose 35 pounds. After two months away from competitive golf, Yin returned this week at the FM Championship for a trial run to see how her game feels and if she believes she’s fit to play in the Netherlands.

Golf.body:
UPDATE: Viktor Hovland birdied three of his final four holes to shoot a 65 in Round 3 and heads into Sunday’s final round of the Tour Championship with a one-shot lead. When it comes to his golf swing, PGA Tour veteran Viktor Hovland is lost. He’s also tied for the lead at the halfway point of the 2026 Tour Championship.

If you feel like those two things shouldn’t go together, you’re not wrong. But Hovland is not your normal pro golfer. And here we are. On Friday evening, after shooting a 66 to move into a tie for the lead at 10 under, Hovland was at his enigmatic best, detailing his frustration with his game and attempting to reconcile his lack of confidence with the fact that he’s in the hunt for the FedEx Cup title.

Golf.body:
The tank looms low on the horizon over the cliffs of Monterey, lurking in the high grass with a distinct sense of foreboding. It takes only a few moments in its presence to realize why.

Inside, the tank is ablaze with energy. The ceilings are low and the light is lower. The space is at once cramped and constantly churning with new people. The atmosphere raises the hair on your forearms, and it’s not immediately clear if the culprit is the icy air-conditioning or the claustrophobia.

Badminton.body:
AirBadminton will make its debut at The World Games 2029 in Karlsruhe, Germany, from 19-29 July after being included among the 36 sports and 62 disciplines confirmed by the International World Games Association (IWGA).

Around 4,000 athletes from more than 100 countries are expected to compete in Karlsruhe, showcasing the very best of The World Games movement. The inclusion marks a significant milestone for AirBadminton, which was launched by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) in May 2019 alongside the specially developed AirShuttle.

Badminton.body:
AirBadminton will make its debut at The World Games 2029 in Karlsruhe, Germany, from 19-29 July after being included among the 36 sports and 62 disciplines confirmed by the International World Games Association (IWGA).

Around 4,000 athletes from more than 100 countries are expected to compete in Karlsruhe, showcasing the very best of The World Games movement. The inclusion marks a significant milestone for AirBadminton, which was launched by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) in May 2019 alongside the specially developed AirShuttle.

Badminton.summary: Weng Hongyang, Wang Zhiyi storm into quarterfinals at BWF China Masters chinadailyasia.com
Badminton.body:
SHENZHEN – Weng Hongyang and Wang Zhiyi advanced to the men's and women's singles quarterfinals respectively at the 2026 BWF China Masters on Thursday. Weng battled past Singapore's Loh Kean Yew 21-18, 11-21, 21-17 in a three-game thriller, but compatriot Lu Guangzu fell to Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn 21-17, 21-12.

Women's singles second seed Wang Zhiyi beat Malaysia's Karupathevan Letshanaa 21-10, 21-8 in just 31 minutes to secure her quarterfinal spot. Young Chinese shuttler Han Qianxi was eliminated in the round of 16, losing to top seed An Se-young of South Korea in straight games.

Badminton.title: China Masters: Underdogs Deliver Upset Bonanza
Badminton.summary: China Masters: Underdogs Deliver Upset Bonanza bwfworldtour.bwfbadminton.com
Badminton.body:
The outsiders seized the spotlight from established names at LI-NING China Masters 2026 on Thursday, with four categories producing unlikely results. The biggest shock came in men’s singles, where Hong Kong China’s Jason Gunawan stunned top seed and newly crowned world No.1 Jonatan Christie 21-16 21-16 in their first meeting.

“I know my opponent had more pressure. I’m the underdog so I just did my best to win every point,” said Gunawan. The 22-year-old revealed preparation was deliberately uncomplicated, with his coach encouraging him to attack rather than allow Christie to settle.

Badminton.title: Shim Yu-jin Falls to Yamaguchi Akane in BWF Masters Round of 16
Badminton.summary: Shim Yu-jin Falls to Yamaguchi Akane in BWF Masters Round of 16 조선일보
Badminton.body:
[OSEN=Ko Sung-hwan Reporter] Shim Yu-jin (27 years old, Incheon International Airport) failed to overcome the wall of Yamaguchi Akane (29), the "pride of Japanese badminton." World No. 16 Shim lost 0-2 (15-21, 16-21) to Yamaguchi (world No. 3) in the women’s singles Round of 16 match at the 2026 BWF World Badminton Federation (BWF) China Masters held at Shenzhen Arena in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, on September 3 (Korean time).

Shim, who advanced by easily defeating Song Shu-yun (Taiwan) 2-0 (21-9, 21-13) in the first round, challenged for her first win against Yamaguchi. She had lost all four previous meetings. Shim struggled to secure even a single game against the global powerhouse, leaving her with lingering regret.

Badminton.title: China Masters: Liu/Hsu Tame World Champs
Badminton.summary: China Masters: Liu/Hsu Tame World Champs BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue found their first test as world champions a painful one as Liu Kuang Heng/Hsu Yin-hui stunned them 23-21 21-10 in just 38 minutes in the LI-NING China Masters 2026 opening round on Wednesday.

Liu/Hsu produced a composed and aggressive display to subdue the French duo, who claimed the world title just two Sundays ago. Trailing 19-17, Liu/Hsu fought back to level the score before saving a game point and eventually closing out the game 23-21. That breakthrough proved decisive – with the pressure shifting firmly onto the French, Liu/Hsu raced through the second game 21-10.

Badminton.title: Lakshya Sen vs Victor Lai live streaming: When and where to watch China Masters 2026
Badminton.summary: Lakshya Sen vs Victor Lai live streaming: When and where to watch China Masters 2026 Sportstar
Badminton.body:
Lakshya Sen will begin his China Masters 2026 campaign against Canada’s Victor Lai on Wednesday, in a men’s singles opener shaped by a late change at the top of the draw. The Indian was originally due to meet newly crowned world champion Alex Lanier of France, but the Frenchman withdrew from the Super 750 event after his title-winning run at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi, handing Lakshya a more familiar test in Lai instead.

The pairing is anything but unknown territory. Lakshya and Lai have already met three times in 2026, including a gruelling contest at the All England Championships that stretched deep into a third game and underlined how evenly matched the two are. Lai arrives with the better recent form, having reached the semifinals at the Worlds, while Lakshya will be looking to respond after a second-round exit in New Delhi to the USA’s Garret Tan.

In the growth of the BWF flagship programme – Shuttle Time – with more than 160 countries implementing the programme, the programme has been delivered and adapted using creative and innovative ways by BWF, Continental Confederations, Member Associations and international partners to meet their particular badminton and social development goals.

Badminton.title: From watching Shin-chan, Doraemon and K-dramas to translating shuttlers' words for the world: How young interpreters found their way to badminton's biggest stage
Badminton.summary: From watching Shin-chan, Doraemon and K-dramas to translating shuttlers' words for the world: How young interpreters found their way to badminton's biggest stage timesofindia.indiatimes.com
Badminton.body:
, players weighed every word as carefully as their drop shots. But beyond the glare of the cameras, another contest was quietly unfolding. Standing a step behind the athletes were the interpreters, almost invisible yet carrying the immense responsibility of ensuring that nuance survived the journey from Mandarin, Japanese or Korean into English.

At a World Championships, where every word can travel as quickly as a smash, a mistranslated phrase can soften conviction, distort the meaning of an entire exchange or, in the worst case, trigger an unintended geopolitical controversy. For the interpreters, getting the words right is only part of the job. The real challenge is ensuring that nothing gets lost in translation.

Badminton.title: Rwanda Project Creates Lasting Impact
Badminton.summary: Rwanda Project Creates Lasting Impact BWF Fansite
Badminton.body:
The Rwanda Badminton Federation’s Badminton Sport for All project, which won the Participation Award at the 2026 Member Association Awards, has demonstrated how sport can be a powerful vehicle for health, inclusion, and community development.

Delivered through schools, community centres and clubs in 42 locations, the initiative engaged over 1,500 participants, including 40 per cent women and girls, besides a significant percentage of those with disabilities.

Competitor News.title: EverPass Media Expands Netflix Partnership to Bring NFL Broadcasts to Venues Nationwide
Competitor News.summary: EverPass Media Expands Netflix Partnership to Bring NFL Broadcasts to Venues Nationwide Ministry of Sport
Competitor News.body:
EverPass Media has secured an expanded multi-year distribution agreement with Netflix to deliver the streaming giant’s complete National Football League content slate to commercial establishments across the United States.

Building on a successful prior collaboration that brought Christmas Day fixtures and live boxing events to hospitality venues, the partnership encompasses high-profile global fixtures, including the upcoming Week 1 Melbourne clash between the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams, the league’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the 2027 NFL Honors ceremony.
